    Breaking: Democrats nominate Jeffries to be House speaker, a historic first

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (928 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that house Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., flanked by House Minority Whip Katherine M.
    • House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries won a closed-door vote of the Democratic caucus Wednesday setting him up to be the nation’s first Black speaker of the House, a historic step that follows Democrats’ staggering election wins earlier this month.
    • According to recent reports, jeffries, who had called for a recorded vote of the more than 250-member caucus that will serve in the next Congress despite facing no confirmed opponent, won decisively, 251-11.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that house Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., flanked by House Minority Whip Katherine M. Clark, D-Mass., and House Democratic Caucus Chair Pete Aguilar, D-Calif., hold a press conference in the Capitol after the House Democratic leadership elections on Wednesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries won a closed-door vote of the Democratic caucus Wednesday setting him up to be the nation’s first Black speaker of the House, a historic step that follows Democrats’ staggering election wins earlier this month.

    According to recent reports, jeffries, who had called for a recorded vote of the more than 250-member caucus that will serve in the next Congress despite facing no confirmed opponent, won decisively, 251-11. The margin suggests Jeffries will easily surpass the necessary 218 votes he will need on the House floor when the full chamber votes in January.

    “It's a high honor and a distinct privilege to stand before the American people today as a Democratic nominee to be the next Speaker of the United States House of Representatives,” Jeffries mentioned at a press conference following the election.

    While Jeffries celebrates his win, he has continued to put an emphasis on unity before he faces what has been deemed the toughest job in Washington. Democrats’ massive majority will give him some margin for maneuvering as he balances the priorities of a complex caucus ranging from moderates to progressives.

    It has been revealed that “Our job is to fight MAGA extremism, not each other,” Jeffries responded when asked about the 11 defections and what they mean for the next Congress. “Fight MAGA extremism, and to get major things done for the American people, and that is what we are going to accomplish together, beginning on January 3rd.”.

    Seven of the 11 members who intended to vote against Jeffries released a statement saying that conversations with leadership are still “ongoing” and that there is “work to be done,” but noting there has been “meaningful progress.” The seven included Reps.- elect Darializa Avilia Chavelier, D-N.Y., Adam Hamawy, D-N.J., Frederick Haynes, D-Texas, Melat Kiros, D-Colo., Donovan McKinney, D-Mich., Chris Rabb, D-Pa., and Claire Valdez, D-N.Y.

    Recent findings suggest that “Whether on Medicare for All, stopping ICE terror, getting money out of politics, or ending the genocide in Gaza, our constituents sent us to Congress with a mandate on these problems,” they wrote. “We have worked to secure commitments from Leader Jeffries in good-faith conversations.”.

    Newly elected House Democrats will meet with former President Barack Obama Wednesday night, where party unity will also be a likely topic.

    “This is the beginning of a new bargain, a new politics where hard work is honored and where people's voice is paramount, and where we have more confidence in the future than nostalgia for the past,” House Minority Whip Katherine M. Clark, D-Mass., noted at the press conference.

    According to recent reports, rep. Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., who made history two decades ago as the nation’s first female speaker, arrived for the vote chanting “Hakeem Jeffries!”, reflecting party leaders’ desire to start the long morning of balloting on a positive note.

    Jeffries' nomination followed the election of current Democratic Caucus Vice Chairman Ted Lieu, D-Calif., to serve as the caucus chair in the next Congress. Separate votes followed Wednesday morning, keeping Jeffries' leadership team intact: Clark, as the upcoming majority leader and Democratic Caucus Chairman Pete Aguilar, D-Calif., as majority whip.

    Industry observers note that at his news conference, Jeffries noted that Clark was also making history as the first woman ever to serve in the position. Aguilar will also be the first Latino to serve as majority whip.

    In a recent development, “We've been looking at people's talents, not a particular gender or race, and I think that's a good thing,” outgoing Rep. Steny H. Hoyer, D-Md., a former majority leader, told reporters ahead of the election.

    Recent findings suggest that “I think Hakeem Jeffries is going to be a good speaker,” Hoyer continued. “He has the confidence of the caucus, and he has a good leadership team that is close knit and very organized.”.

    Jeffries expressed confidence in the weeks leading up to his securing the top Democratic spot in the House, brushing aside questions about incoming members who had said they remained “undecided” ahead of the election.

    Pelosi was nominated for speaker by acclamation ahead of her first election to the position in 2007. But Jeffries’ allies portrayed his decision to move forward with a recorded vote as a show of strength after a group of incoming progressives had floated forcing a recorded vote in the internal leadership race.

    It has been revealed that the entire leadership team will be tested despite their numerical advantage over Republicans by the same internal tensions facing Senate Democrats, where current Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., is being challenged for leadership of the majority by Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md.

    Jeffries said Tuesday that the approach to the caucus vote mirrored the caucus’ 2018 transition from minority to majority, giving members an opportunity to weigh in on who was best positioned to lead based on their “track record, experience and vision.”.

    Jeffries has already outlined some of his top priorities of his speakership such as a hefty healthcare agenda, immigration legislation, and a multitude of investigations into the Trump administration.

    He also signaled Wednesday another area where his party’s restive base is likely to close ranks: oversight.

    “House Democrats will hold the crooks accountable, not for partisan reasons, but for patriotic ones,” he noted at his news conference.

    #123624. Tech Report: Why British Airways Decided To Replace Its Longstanding Quadjet Fleet With Large Twin-Engine Airbus A350-1000s

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1503 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Simpleflying ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Why British Airways Decided To Replace Its Longstanding Quadjet Fleet With Large Twin-Engine Airbus A350-1000s

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1503 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that while the passenger Boeing 747-400 is most closely associated with Lufthansa today, it had long been British Airways that was the world's largest operator of this aircraft, the most successful variant of the iconic 747.
    • However, all good things must come to an end, and the carrier's entire fleet of 747-400s was retired during the COVID-19 pandemic.
    • At the time, the main aircraft that British Airways was using to replace the 747-400 was the Airbus A350-1000, a twin-engined carbon-composite widebody that British Airways now operates 18 examples of.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that while the passenger Boeing 747-400 is most closely associated with Lufthansa today, it had long been British Airways that was the world's largest operator of this aircraft, the most successful variant of the iconic 747. At one point, British Airways operated 57 747-400s, and these planes flew all over the world while simultaneously serving as the British flag carrier's flagship aircraft and its largest widebody fleet.

    However, all good things must come to an end, and the carrier's entire fleet of 747-400s was retired during the COVID-19 pandemic. British Airways was already gradually retiring its 747-400s by the time the pandemic struck, but the onset of the global healt crisis expedited this process.

    At the time, the main aircraft that British Airways was using to replace the 747-400 was the Airbus A350-1000, a twin-engined carbon-composite widebody that British Airways now operates 18 examples of. While the A350-1000 is large and hugely capable, its strengths are actually quite different from what the 747-400 once offered.

    Recent findings suggest that with such a large fleet of 747-400s, British Airways divided its aircraft into subfleets that featured different layouts. In the fleet's later years, Planespotters.net reveals that the airline had two main layouts for its 747-400s. One configuration featured 14 First seats, 52 Club World seats, 36 World Traveller Plus seats, and 235 World Traveller seats, for a total of 337 seats.

    According to recent reports, most of British Airways' 747-400s featured this layout leading up to the 2010s, but this fleet was reduced before the type was fully retired. The other layout that was in use at the time of the type's retirement featured 14 First seats, 86 Club World seats, 30 World Traveller Plus seats, and 145 World Traveller seats, for a total of 275 seats.

    Recent findings suggest that this is an exceptionally low amount for the massive 747-400, and it's entirely because of the massive Club World business class cabin. This is the configuration to serve destinations such as Fresh York, while the denser layout could be used for a wider variety of destinations, such as Las Vegas.

    Recent findings suggest that while the premium-heavy subfleet was smaller at one point, British Airways retired fewer of them in the 2010s, and a majority of the 747s retired during COVID featured this layout. In 2019, British Airways began taking delivery of the Airbus A350-1000, and crucially, the carrier used these to replace its denser 747-400s rather than the premium-heavy subfleet. To replace those aircraft, British Airways had other aircraft in mind.

    British Airways configures its A350-1000s with 56 Club Suites, 56 World Traveller Plus seats, 219 World Traveller seats, and no First cabin, for a total of 331 seats. This is almost the same number of seats as the airline's 747-400s with the denser layout, which had a First cabin, fewer Club World seats, fewer World Traveller Plus seats, and more World Traveller seats.

    It has been revealed that the aircraft still has relatively large premium cabins and is used where the carrier needs a high-capacity aircraft, but not necessarily one with First. The A350-1000 has become known for being an exceptionally fuel-efficient aircraft with longer range than almost any other type in service today, and with the ability to carry meaningful payload across long distances too.

    Recent findings suggest that for British Airways, however, the main appeal of the A350-1000 was its combination of size and fuel efficiency. It's significantly larger than a Boeing 787-10, while it burns less fuel than the similarly-sized Boeing 777-300ER, and the type is regularly seen in destinations such as Philadelphia, Las Vegas, Phoenix, and more. Some of the places where British Airways deploys the A350-1000 can have a price-sensitive customer base.

    As such, the A350-1000's low operating costs are extremely beneficial. Meanwhile, the plane can still earn substantial premium revenue on services to major business destinations such as São Paulo and Hong Kong. The A350-1000 is highly effective in this role, and British Airways holds six more orders for the type, but it wasn't the only aircraft type that British Airways used to replace the 747-400.

    British Airways took delivery of 12 Airbus A380-800s from 2013 to 2016, which replaced part of the airline's 747-400 fleet. Because of how slot-constrained British Airways' main hub at London Heathrow Airport (LHR) is, the A380's increased capacity is ideal for the airline, considering that it's not always easy to add another frequency.

    According to recent reports, the A380 offers significantly more seats in Club World, World Traveller Plus, and World Traveller, with British Airways deploying the A380 to destinations like Los Angeles, San Francisco, and Johannesburg. The A380 works well for British Airways on high-demand routes where the airline operates limited daily frequencies.

    Meanwhile, to directly succeed the premium 747-400s on routes with high business demand, British Airways ordered 16 777-300ERs with eight First seats, 76 Club Suites, 40 World Traveller Plus seats, and 132 World Traveller seats, for a total of 256 seats. The 777-300ER seats fewer passengers than the 747-400 but has much lower operating costs, while the A380 seats significantly more passengers.

    In addition to these aircraft, British Airways also planned to use the Boeing 777-9 to replace the last of its 747-400s. This ended up not occurring, due to delays with the 777-9 and the COVID-19 pandemic resulting in the early retirement of the 747-400 fleet.

    The original retirement date set by British Airways for the 747-400 was 2024, by which point the airline would have received a significant number of 777-9s. As a whole, British Airways intended to use four aircraft types to replace the 747-400 for different missions, three of which are twinjets.

    It has been revealed that the 747-400 was the largest airliner in the world when it first came out in 1989, and it also had the longest range of any commercial jet in service. At the same time, the aircraft was a major technological step forward for the 747 platform, and it was also efficient for its time. Airlines bought the 747-400 in droves, while British Airways used its huge fleet to perform multiple types of missions and serve a variety of roles.

    At the time, it did these roles better than any other aircraft type in service for British Airways' needs. However, as time went on, Airbus and Boeing introduced fresh aircraft similar in size to the 747-400, while also having true ultra-long-haul range. The 777-300ER entered service in 2004, while the A350-1000 entered service in 2018.

    Industry observers note that most importantly, however, these two airliners sip fuel in comparison to the 747-400 as a result of their twin-engine configuration, reduced weight, and more advanced aerodynamics. The 747-400 is outdated, having entered service 37 years ago, and there are multiple types that can do its job better. The A380 is the exception, as it is a massive quadjet that seats significantly more passengers than the 747-400.

    In a recent development, the aircraft delivers superior economics to the 747-400, and when full, the aircraft can be incredibly profitable. However, it's also risky to operate an aircraft with such high operating costs and upwards of 450 seats, while the 777-300ER and A350-1000 are just as or more economical to operate. Still, British Airways does have a clear need for an aircraft this large given its constraints at LHR.

    In 2019, the International Airlines Group placed an order for 18 777-9s with 24 options, all of which were to be allocated to British Airways. IAG later converted six options to firm orders, giving British Airways 24 777-9s. Originally, these planes would have been the final replacement for the 747-400, although COVID and the 777-9's delays have changed these prepares.

    This aircraft was meant to enter service in 2020, but this has been pushed back to 2027 at the earliest, while British Airways' examples may only start coming in 2028. The 777-300ER and A350-1000 can effectively replace the 747-400 by being somewhat smaller but far more efficient.

    The 777-9, however, is stretched compared to the 777-300ER, and it has nearly as much interior floor space as the 747-400. What's more, the aircraft has a fresh carbon-composite wing and new General Electric GE9X engines, cutting fuel burn further. This makes it an extremely cost-effective aircraft, and its size makes it the most direct replacement for the 747-400. BA's layout for the 777-9 has not been revealed.

    Found an error? Send it info@simpleflying.com so it can be corrected.

    Sources indicate that however, it is known that the aircraft will feature an all-fresh First suite, which is also currently being retrofitted on the A380. In addition, British Airways tends to favor large premium cabins, a practice which will likely carry over with the 777-9. The actual routes that the 777-9 will operate are also unknown, but as the 747s have been fully retired for years, the long-awaited arrival of the 777-9 should allow for more long-haul growth since they're not replacing a type currently in the fleet.

    Breaking: Southwest Airlines Plus Card Review: Modest Benefits For A Low Annual Fee

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2130 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Southwest Airlines and Chase have a great portfolio of co-branded credit cards at a variety of “price points” (and by that I mean annual fees).
    • In my Southwest Plus Card review, I’ll cover the benefits and explain why now is a good time to consider this card if you want to use credit card spending to earn the Companion Pass.
    • Link: Learn more about the Southwest Rapid Rewards® Plus Credit Card.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Southwest Airlines and Chase have a great portfolio of co-branded credit cards at a variety of “price points” (and by that I mean annual fees). In this post, I’d like to take a closer look at the Southwest Rapid Rewards® Plus Credit Card, which is Southwest Airlines’ lowest annual fee credit card.

    In my Southwest Plus Card review, I’ll cover the benefits and explain why now is a good time to consider this card if you want to use credit card spending to earn the Companion Pass. I’ll also explain why other Southwest cards can be better, and share a great alternative to earning Southwest Rapid Rewards points altogether.

    Link: Learn more about the Southwest Rapid Rewards® Plus Credit Card.

    Before I get into my Southwest Plus Card review, here are some of the key card details:.

    Here are my thoughts on the Southwest Plus Card’s pros and cons:.

    Let’s take a look at the Southwest Plus Card‘s welcome bonus, annual fee, and eligibility rules, as these are some of the most important factors to take into account if you’re considering applying.

    In a recent development, the Southwest Plus Card is offering a limited time welcome bonus: Earn 80,000 bonus points after spending $1,000 on purchases in the first 3 months from account opening. This is one of the higher bonuses I’ve seen on this card recently, making now a particularly good time to apply.

    Recent findings suggest that rapid Rewards is a revenue-based frequent flyer program, and based on my latest miles & points valuations, I consider Rapid Rewards points to be worth 1.2 cents each. So to me, the points from this welcome offer are worth $960.

    In terms of Southwest credit card eligibility, the card isn’t available to anyone who currently has a Southwest Rapid Rewards personal card, or anyone who has received a welcome bonus on a Southwest Rapid Rewards personal card in the past 24 months. However, you are eligible if you have a Southwest business credit card.

    Beyond the restrictions related to which Southwest cards you have, keep in mind the general restrictions for Chase card approvals, including the 5/24 rule. However, there are increasing data points of this no longer being consistently enforced.

    Another rule worth mentioning here involves how Southwest credit card welcome bonuses help you earn the Companion Pass, which lets you bring a companion with you on flights (both cash and award tickets) and pay just taxes and fees.

    For a long time now, the points earned as part of Southwest credit card welcome bonuses have counted towards the 135,000 qualifying points needed to earn the Companion Pass. But starting soon, credit card welcome bonuses will no longer count toward qualification.

    Recent findings suggest that you’ll need to apply for a card by December 2, 2026, for your welcome bonus to count toward the Companion Pass for a final time. So apply for this card now if you’re hoping to earn that perk with the help of credit card spending.

    Recent findings suggest that now is also your last chance to get an annual boost of 10,000 Companion Pass qualifying points as a Southwest credit card holder. Starting next year, instead of a boost of 10,000 TQPs for having a Southwest card, you’ll get 10,000 TQPs if your TQP balance is 130,000 by December 31, 2027. That would be enough to get you to Platinum status, which will include unlimited Companion Pass trips as a benefit.

    Recent findings suggest that this change eliminates the easiest way to earn this valuable benefit, and it’s not the only new rule: referral bonuses, anniversary points, bonus points from spending, and partner spending won’t count toward the Companion Pass either. In fact, Southwest’s rolling the Companion Pass into its highest elite tier, Platinum, and requiring either 140,000 TQPs or 100 qualifying flights to earn it.

    The Southwest Plus Card has a $99 annual fee, and you can add authorized people to the card at no extra cost.

    $99 is the lowest annual fee of any Southwest Airlines credit card. Looking at the high end, Southwest’s personal cards have annual fees of up to $229, and Southwest’s business cards have annual fees of up to $299.

    The Southwest Plus Card has no foreign transaction fees, so it’s a solid card to use for purchases abroad.

    As far as the Southwest Plus Card‘s rewards structure goes, the card offers the following:.

    Since I value Southwest Rapid Rewards points at 1.2 cents each, I think you get an effective return of 2.4% on purchases that qualify for 2x points, and a 1.2% return on everything else.

    It’s nice that the card has some bonus categories, though there are ultimately more rewarding cards out there for everyday spending. Plus, a few of the non-Southwest bonus categories have an annual cap, which limits how useful this card is for maximizing your return on gas station and grocery store purchases.

    I have a dedicated post that covers how to redeem Southwest Rapid Rewards points for maximum value, but let’s briefly look at how you can use the points you earn from the Southwest Plus Card.

    In a recent development, rapid Rewards is a revenue-based frequent flyer program, meaning that the value you get from your points is tied to the cash cost of Southwest tickets. There are a few different levels, ranging from Basic tickets to Choice Extra fares, so the exact value can vary a bit.

    In a recent development, basic award fares tend to offer the best redemption value. You’ll also usually get the best value on international Southwest routes to destinations like Costa Rica and Aruba. I’ve been able to get about 2.0 cents per point on these redemptions.

    Industry observers note that starting in spring 2027, Southwest will add points earning and redemption opportunities with select airline partners, which should make your Rapid Rewards points more valuable for international travel. The planned partners include Icelandair, China Airlines, and Etihad Airways — I look forward to seeing how these add value to the program.

    In a recent development, one great thing about the Southwest Rapid Rewards program is that there are no change or cancellation fees, and rebooking a fare when the price drops gets you a refund equal to any difference in points. Just note that Basic fares can only be changed by upgrading to a higher fare bundle, so for a cheaper Basic award you’d cancel and rebook rather than change.

    It has been revealed that the Southwest Plus Card offers some benefits that could make the card worth keeping long term. However, this is also Southwest’s lowest annual fee card, so it doesn’t have the most benefits. What are the ongoing perks of having this card?

    Recent findings suggest that the Southwest Plus Card gets the primary cardholder and up to eight additional passengers on the same reservation a first checked bag at no additional cost. Checked bags on Southwest cost $45 each way, so this can save you up to $90 roundtrip on checked bag fees per person. So with just one roundtrip flight per year, this benefit can almost offset the annual fee.

    According to recent reports, southwest now charges for seat selection, so it’s helpful that the Southwest Plus Card includes complimentary standard seat selection starting 48 hours out from departure. This perk is based on availability, and it could save you around $20 to $40 per flight.

    Another Southwest benefit is early boarding. You’ll be able to board with Group 5, or earlier if you have elite status or a fare or seat type that qualifies you for an earlier boarding group. Southwest has eight total boarding groups, so while there are several ahead of Group 5, it’s better than boarding last.

    Each year on your Southwest Plus Card cardmember anniversary, you’ll get a 10% promo code that applies to Southwest flights. Just note that this discount excludes Basic fares.

    Sources indicate that on your Southwest Plus Card cardmember anniversary every year, you’ll receive 3,000 bonus points. Southwest Rapid Rewards is a revenue-based frequent flyer program, and you’ll typically need 83 Rapid Rewards points for every dollar of airfare you book. In other words, those 3,000 Rapid Rewards points should get you around $36 worth of airfare on Southwest annually.

    As part of an overhaul of the Rapid Rewards program, Southwest is simplifying TQP earning on credit cards. Starting in 2027, every dollar spent on a co-branded Southwest credit card will earn you one TQP. In other words, $35K in spending would earn you Silver, $65K in spending would earn you Gold, and $140K in spending would earn you Platinum.

    This earning rate is the same across cards, so this isn’t specific to the Southwest Plus Card.

    Recent findings suggest that the Southwest Plus Card offers 25% savings on inflight purchases of Wi-Fi and drinks. Simply pay with your card, and you’ll automatically receive a statement credit for that amount.

    The Southwest Plus Card offers a variety of travel & purchase protection benefits, including:.

    You’ll want to check the cardmember agreement for the full terms & conditions associated with these benefits.

    One of the great features of Chase cards is access to Chase Offers, which provides savings on purchases with all kinds of retailers. This program has saved me a significant amount of money.

    The Southwest Plus Card is a solid entry-level airline credit card. If you want a credit card from Southwest and want an annual fee as low as possible, then this card could make sense to you.

    You’ll receive a 3,000-point bonus on your cardmember anniversary every year, and 25% savings on inflight purchases. The free checked bag benefit can save you $90 on a roundtrip and the complimentary standard seat selection benefit can add up rapidly after a few flights. These perks can more than justify the annual fee, and that’s not even accounting for the massive welcome bonus.

    However, there are other options that I think can make more sense.

    Sources indicate that if your main reason for considering the Southwest Rapid Rewards Plus Card is to earn points for Southwest award flights, you might be better off skipping a Southwest co-branded credit card altogether and just earning Chase Ultimate Rewards points. You can transfer Chase points to Southwest to book flights, and cards like the Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card (learn more) have stronger earning categories and benefits overall.

    You can also redeem Ultimate Rewards points with other travel partners, not just Southwest, so this option gives you more flexibility.

    Sources indicate that the Southwest Rapid Rewards® Premier Credit Card (learn more) is one step up from the Southwest Plus Card, with a $149 annual fee. Here’s a look at its key perks:.

    There’s also the Southwest Rapid Rewards® Priority Credit Card (learn more), the most premium personal Southwest card with a $229 annual fee. If you want as many Southwest perks as possible, this is a better pick.

    The Southwest Priority Card’s main perks include:.

    So you’re getting a higher return of 4.8% on Southwest spending on the Priority Card, based on my valuations, and better complimentary seat selection and upgrade options.

    Recent findings suggest that if you want a Southwest Rapid Rewards business credit card in place of or in addition to a personal card, I highly recommend considering the Southwest® Rapid Rewards® Performance Business Credit Card (learn more). The Southwest Performance Business Card offers the following benefits, which make it the best Southwest credit card, in my opinion:.

    The Southwest Performance Business Card offers a lot of points, and more perks overall than other Southwest cards.

    Sources indicate that the Southwest Plus Card is a good entry-level credit card for someone who wants to earn Rapid Rewards points without paying a high annual fee. It’s not the most valuable Southwest credit card in the lineup, but its benefits and strong welcome bonus make it a good option at this price point.

    #123621. Dems express ‘points of anxiety’ over Trump’s summit with Putin and Xi

    Dems express ‘points of anxiety’ over Trump’s summit with Putin and Xi

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1206 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • President Donald Trump prepares to shake hands with Russian President Vladimir Putin as China's President Xi Jinping looks on before the welcome banquet at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday, Nov.
    • Some Senate Democrats have heartburn about President Donald Trump’s planned Thursday meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping, but Republicans counter by saying he could get the Russian and Chinese leaders to budge on a list of challenges even as he appears politically weakened at home.
    • Trump arrived Wednesday in China’s Shenzhen economic zone on the banks of the Pearl River ahead of a high-level summit that was ostensibly slated to focus on paring each countries’ nuclear arsenal.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    President Donald Trump prepares to shake hands with Russian President Vladimir Putin as China's President Xi Jinping looks on before the welcome banquet at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. (Iori Sagisawa / POOL / AFP via Getty Images).

    Some Senate Democrats have heartburn about President Donald Trump’s planned Thursday meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping, but Republicans counter by saying he could get the Russian and Chinese leaders to budge on a list of challenges even as he appears politically weakened at home.

    Trump arrived Wednesday in China’s Shenzhen economic zone on the banks of the Pearl River ahead of a high-level summit that was ostensibly slated to focus on paring each countries’ nuclear arsenal. But before he left, Trump signaled the three-way talks also likely would include the artificial intelligence race, Moscow’s bloody war with Ukraine, global trade and his standoff with Iran.

    Industry observers note that the U.S. commander in chief’s tendency to sound deferential to Putin and habit of referring to Xi as a personal “friend” concerns many congressional Democrats. But Trump’s GOP allies on Capitol Hill, despite this month’s midterm election losses, still describe him as a dealmaker who has a chance to use his final years to bend Putin and Xi toward U.S. interests.

    Rick Scott, a Florida Republican who sits on the Senate Armed Services and Foreign Relations committees, stated Tuesday he was hopeful that Trump could make some progress on at least one problem with the Russian and Chinese leaders.

    Sources indicate that “As we all know, China and Russia want to destroy our way of life,” he said. “But it would be great to reduce … nuclear stockpiles and make sure we're not going to ever get attacked.

    In a recent development, still, Scott sounded skeptical about two world leaders Trump has tried to keep close during his two terms. “But do I trust Xi or Putin? No, they're a bunch of liars.” Asked if he worries Trump might trust them too much, Scott replied: “I don't think he trusts him any more than I do. … I'm glad the president's trying. Hope springs eternal. But do I actually really believe something good's going to come out of it? I don't.”.

    Outgoing House Armed Services Vice Chair Rob Wittman, R-Va., mentioned part of Trump’s talks on Thursday “should be to make sure the world is a safer place, to make sure we don't have aggressive behavior like Russia in an unprovoked attack against Ukraine.

    “They ought to be talking about how they don't do those sorts of things, how they don't threaten their neighbors, how they don't try to intimidate through the assertion of force that they ought to be able to work together to make sure we assure a safe globe,” remarked Wittman, who lost his reelection race earlier this month.

    That comment came one day after Trump told reporters as he left the White House for Asia that he sees Putin “backing down a little bit” in his conduct of the war with Ukraine.

    Recent findings suggest that “I think he could be tougher. I think he could be a lot tougher, frankly,” Trump said Monday. “I think he's backing down.”.

    Those kinds of deferential remarks about the Russian leader are a substantial reason why some Democrats have heartburn about Thursday’s meeting.

    Senate Armed Services member Mazie K. Hirono, D-Hawaii, said Tuesday that she’s concerned about the Shenzhen summit because “I’m not sure what’s going to pop out of [Trump’s] mouth next — especially for a meeting with two guys he clearly likes.”.

    In a recent development, sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., also a member of the Armed Services and Foreign Relations committees, mentioned he has “high hopes” for the trilateral meeting — but “maybe not high expectations.”.

    Sources indicate that “I have some points of anxiety. I'm nervous about any discussion about Ukraine that doesn't involve the Ukrainians. And, so, some of the advance to this is like, ‘We're going to talk about ending the Ukraine war.’ You can't do that without Ukraine at the table,” Kaine stated. “So the desire to bring about more peace and stability, that's a good thing to talk about. But no conditions about Ukraine and ending that war without them at the table? Not so sure about that.”.

    During remarks Tuesday on the Senate floor, Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer criticized what he described as Trump’s misplaced priorities.

    “Enforcement of the upcoming rules restricting China’s access to our most sensitive AI chips should start today,” the New York Democrat remarked, adding that Trump should focus more of his Asia swing on securing commitments from U.S. allies to block China from gaining an upper hand in the AI technology race.

    Trump touted just that on Tuesday during remarks in Manila at a U.S.-Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit in the Philippines.

    “Since I returned to office, we've made major trade deals with Malaysia, Cambodia, Indonesia, as well as Japan, South Korea, and almost everybody, frankly, at the table,” he said. “And we've made many other vital agreements across the region spanning energy, critical minerals and technology.”.

    But on Wednesday, Trump appeared to have pivoted to the trip’s main event.

    He stood beside Xi at an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen and smiled as Putin approached. Trump extended his hand and shook Putin’s as the Chinese leader looked on.

    Scott, a Trump ally in the Senate, noted Tuesday he sees the president “trying to build relationships to try to make sure we don't end up at war [because] he doesn't like war.”.

    Trump signaled Monday that he might press Xi for details on an alleged Chinese spy who had an affair with Nvidia founder Jensen Huang, costing the AI mogul his job as the organization’s president and CEO. He also remarked he could bring up Nvidia’s sales of sophisticated microchips that many lawmakers — Republican and Democrat — want to ensure remain in the U.S. for domestic AI development.

    Industry observers note that the administration’s response to the turmoil at Nvidia, with Trump even suggesting he'd support Huang returning as CEO, is a rare area where Republicans have expressed concern publicly. House Energy and Commerce Committee Chair Brett Guthrie, R-Kent., wrote to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Wednesday seeking information about “the implementation of federal laws governing technology exports, in particular the application of export controls relating to semiconductor chips, the effect of which has a broad impact on America’s race with China to artificial intelligence (AI) dominance and the ability of U.S. companies to set global technology standards.”.

    Heather Williams, director of the Project on Nuclear Problems at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, wrote this week that for the three leaders, the “path is fraught with challenges.”.

    Sources indicate that “Putin could diplomatically outmaneuver the Trump administration and make any progress on nuclear issues dependent on undermining Western support to Ukraine,” she wrote in an analysis for the Washington, D.C.-based think tank. “Even the optics of Trump and Putin negotiating while the war continues and as Russia ramps up missile strikes on Ukrainian civilian targets could be interpreted as undermining U.S. values.”.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, I’ve never been one to take the easy road, so I thought I’d bite the bullet and talk about my love for Delta in what you might call a baptism of fire. Before I jump in, I’m not here screaming that Delta is the best US airline. Far from it. Rather, I’m explaining why, as someone who is not based in the US, Delta is my go-to airline.

    This year, Delta has nudged up to fourth most-flown of the 94 airlines I’ve tried out over the years, and I’d like to share a little bit about why.

    It has been revealed that starting from the ground, I am a big fan of what Delta is doing with its lounges. Stepping inside one of Delta’s newer Sky Clubs, you feel like you’re in the lobby bar of a luxury hotel rather than the corporate canteen-style spaces offered by competitors.

    I know these newer lounges aren’t in every airport yet — Honolulu (HNL) is a notable exception — but lately I’ve found myself enjoying them before the majority of my latest Delta flights departing from a US airport.

    Don’t get me started on the Delta One Lounges: I’ve visited locations at LAX and JFK, and these are without a doubt my favorite airline lounges in the US.

    Stepping onboard, I actually like the planes. In recent times, I’ve flown mainly on its Airbus A320 family aircraft, a few Boeing 757s (which I love), and once on a Boeing 767-300 from Honolulu to LAX.

    I like how they’ve all had seatback screens, I’ve never had an glitch using my SkyMiles account to access the fast free WiFi (it’s decent, even though it’s not Starlink), and I’ve never felt uncomfortable on one of Delta’s planes.

    I also have to say, I’ve always had pleasant, if not better-than-your-average service when flying Delta.

    I love a good redemption as much as the next frequent flyer. However, our credit cards in the UK earn us far fewer points than those in the US, so for me, redeeming points is the exception, not the norm.

    As such, I don’t hate on Delta’s SkyMiles for its mostly sky-high redemption rates. Even if finding a one-way in Delta One from Rio or São Paulo to Latest York for less than 470,000 miles is almost impossible.

    Besides, I credit my Delta flights to my Flying Blue account, which is therefore home to my SkyTeam elite status and miles earned on Delta and all other SkyTeam airlines.

    Neither do I fly often enough nor have the funds to unlock top-tier status in all three alliances. Aside from the Virgin Atlantic Gold status I got from a status match and my BA Silver, which expires in April, Flying Blue is the only program whose status I’m actively chasing.

    In a recent development, as a direct result of Air France and KLM’s membership in the SkyTeam alliance, I actively choose to fly other SkyTeam airlines, such as Delta. Also, thanks to the relationship between Delta and fellow SkyTeam member Aeroméxico, I’ve managed to find great-value cash fares on several occasions when planning travel between Mexico and Canada or the US.

    It has been revealed that I actually used to be a die-hard American boy until the BA Club was sabotaged. In terms of lounges, aircraft comfort, complimentary amenities (like seat back screens and Wi-Fi), and service, Delta has felt like an upgrade.

    For what it’s worth, if status had nothing to do with it, I’d still choose Delta.

    Industry observers note that my experience with American, Delta, and United has mainly been on domestic flights around the US, including transcons. In fact, I’ve never flown Delta One, American Flagship, or United Polaris on long-haul international flights. Who knows, my top three could reshuffle once I’ve tried and tested each of those. Maybe I’ll have to have a word with Ben about this….

    I know Delta gets a bad rep, but honestly I have only had pleasant experiences when flying the airline over the years. As long as I’m being loyal to SkyTeam, it will remain my preference when traveling to or around the US (unless it’s from the UK; then I’m team Virgin).

    Recent findings suggest that I’m going to make it a priority to fly each of American, Delta, and United’s best international long-haul products over the coming months. Watch this space for my thoughts on flying those for the first time, and to see whether Delta remains my US number one.

    I’m curious, what do you love or hate about Delta?

    #123617. 5 Aircraft That Pilots Say Are The Most Technologically Advanced

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1586 w)

    5 Aircraft That Pilots Say Are The Most Technologically Advanced

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1586 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • From enormous airliners to business and fighter jets the cutting-edge aerospace technology of 2026 is pushing the limits of automation, aerodynamics, and more.
    • Pilots praise the Gulfstream G700 for bringing the same level of automation found in large airliners to the world of private aviation.
    • The G700 is also acclaimed for providing 'superhuman' visibility in poor weather through its Combined Vision System.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    From enormous airliners to business and fighter jets the cutting-edge aerospace technology of 2026 is pushing the limits of automation, aerodynamics, and more. Across these platforms, the theme is a move toward enhanced situational awareness and reduced pilot fatigue through automation that acts as a partner rather than just a tool. Collectively, the five incredible aircraft in this article represent the pinnacle of modern flight deck design.

    Pilots praise the Gulfstream G700 for bringing the same level of automation found in large airliners to the world of private aviation. The Symmetry Flight Deck introduces several innovations, like linked sidesticks with tactile feedback for pilot and copilot, ten touchscreen displays, and dual heads-up displays.

    The G700 is also acclaimed for providing 'superhuman' visibility in poor weather through its Combined Vision System. Unlike the Airbus A350, where the pilot's and co-pilot's sidesticks move independently, the G700 features electronically linked active control sidesticks. The non-flying pilot can feel exactly what the other is doing, a critical safety feature for coordination in flight.

    These sticks also move on their own when the autopilot is engaged, for a visual and physical cue of how the computer is flying the plane. The HUDs provide unparalleled visibility under any conditions by merging enhanced video from infrared cameras with a synthetic 3D map view of terrain into a single composite view outside the cockpit.

    In a recent development, combined with the Predictive Landing Performance System that calculates exactly where the aircraft will stop on the runway before it even touches down, the G700 is the gold standard for safety in private aviation. Further empowering the pilots to perform to the best of their ability in any situation is a myriad of anti-fatigue technologies.

    Recent findings suggest that the cabin is pressurized to just 2,840 feet, even though the jet can fly up to 51,000 feet, which is far higher than most jetliners. This means pilots arrive with significantly more oxygen in their blood and far better alertness. The air is also never recirculated. It is completely replaced with fresh, sterilized air every two to three minutes.

    Recent findings suggest that the A380 was the first aircraft designed to be completely paperless. Pilots use an Onboard Information System to access all manuals, charts, and performance calculators on dedicated screens. The electronic flight bag has become a popular feature on latest jets to offer this same convenience, all thanks to the pioneering A380 flight deck.

    It is also equipped with sidestick controls and optional HUDs, drawing on experience from Airbus Defense. Removing the traditional central control yoke also created a spacious, open workspace. The cockpit features eight large LCD screens, and pilots interact with these screens using a trackball-style cursor located on the center pedestal.

    It has been revealed that the A380’s navigation display indicates a detailed, zoomable map of airport layouts, helping pilots navigate complex taxiway networks. To help maneuver the world's largest commercial jet, pilots have live video feeds from a tail-fin camera and a nose-gear camera displayed on the cockpit screens.

    It has been revealed that the A380's flight deck introduced several industry-firsts that set it apart from earlier jets, which have not only made pilot workloads easier, but the jet is described as surprisingly agile and stable, despite weighing over 500 tons. Automation also makes it one of the safest jets ever made. One of the ways it does this is because the sidesticks are not mechanically linked.

    It has been revealed that if both pilots move them at once, the system sums up the inputs unless one pilot takes priority by pressing a red button. The A380 uses Normal Law automation. If a pilot pulls the sidestick all the way back, the computer will only allow the plane to climb at its maximum safe angle: it simply refuses to stall the aircraft. The A380 also pioneered a specialized automation feature called Brake-to-Vacate.

    In a recent development, A fixed glass plate or heads-up display is necessary for older fighter aircraft, but not the F-35. The pilot loses their flight data if they turn their head away. Pilots on a Boeing F/A-18 Super Hornet or F-15 Eagle are required to manually install heavy night vision goggles that limit their field of vision.

    The HUD in the F-35 follows the pilot's eyes instead of being a piece of glass on the dashboard. It makes use of a virtual screen that is displayed on the pilot's visor. The F-35's computers combine radar sensor data with targeting systems, electronic warfare sensors, and a data network to create a single 'fused picture.'.

    Industry observers note that if an enemy plane is 50 miles away, the pilot sees a small green square exactly where it is, even if it is obscured from view. Because it tracks head movement, the HUD is visible whether the pilot is looking ahead, sideways, or down through the plane's floor. The Distributed Aperture System plays an crucial role in making this happen.

    Recent findings suggest that it allows you to see through the floor using a set of six infrared cameras placed in the jet's fuselage in 360 degrees. When the pilot glances down, the system immediately sends video from the bottom cameras to the visor. The F-35's helmet even includes night vision embedded into the frontal camera, which can be triggered rapidly with a button. Gina Sabric, Commander of the 10th Air Force, said that:.

    "The F-35 is the aircraft to take into combat. It's the quarterback of the entire fight.".

    According to recent reports, the F-35's cockpit even has speech-recognition technology that lets pilots issue instructions simply by speaking, like changing radio frequencies or other simple tasks. All major systems and weapon controls are incorporated into the control stick and engine throttle, allowing the pilot to operate the aircraft without releasing the flying controls.

    In a recent development, airbus used extensive input from aircrew to develop what it calls the "most advanced cockpit on the market." The glass cockpit has six large displays laid out in a wide array to ensure both pilots can easily see every data point. Unlike Boeing's commercial aircraft, which have a conventional yoke, the A350XWB features a sidestick control as found in many fighter jets.

    Sources indicate that the absence of a central yoke also allows for a large fold-out table at each seat. These include an integrated keyboard on the reverse side for faster data entry into the flight computers. The A350 is famous for its cockpit window design with large, curved windows that offer a panoramic view and even a 'sunglasses' feature that significantly reduces both glare and blind spots.

    It has been revealed that adding to that military-inspired piece of ergonomic technology are heads-up displays that project critical flight data directly into the pilot's line of sight out of the windshield. Some pilots refer to stepping onto the flight deck of an A350 as akin to stepping into a spaceship because of the impressive flight deck design, but also because of the computer power it contains.

    Recent findings suggest that the side displays even have touchscreens to allow the aircrew to quickly reference the highest priority information. Airbus avionics even have a built-in strict safety net that can override the pilots to prevent accidents. The A350 will physically not allow a pilot to perform dangerous maneuvers, such as stalling the aircraft or banking beyond 67 degrees.

    It treats pilot input as a 'request' that the computer verifies for safety. The autopilot feature can actively dampen turbulence while its highly flexible wings help physically absorb the shock. The FMS will automatically make emergency descents smoother and easier after pilots initiate one and help exit the runway at a specific taxiway using 'brake-to-vacate' automation.

    Many pilots and industry professionals laud Boeing for its intuitive pilot-assisting fly-by-wire system, excellent avionics that process immense amounts of data for aircrew and maintainers, and an exceptional navigation system. Required Navigation Performance 0.1 is an advanced navigation capability that allows the Boeing 787 Dreamliner to maintain its flight path with extreme precision.

    Recent findings suggest that the flight deck was designed with significant input from pilots to reduce workload and enhance situational awareness. Dual HUDs are standard on every 787 to project critical flight data into the pilot's direct line of sight, allowing for safer takeoffs and landings in low-visibility conditions. The cockpit also features five 15-inch screens, offering more than double the display space of older models like the 777.

    Its acclaimed fly-by-wire controls are complemented by an advanced electronic flight bag of charts and navigation data, as well as automated smooth-ride technology that detects and counters turbulence automatically. Unlike standard GPS navigation, RNP systems include performance monitoring and alerting.

    According to recent reports, this automatically notifies pilots if the navigation accuracy drops below the required threshold. The aircraft is kept within 0.1 nautical miles, or about 600 feet, of its centerline for at least 95% of the flight time under the RNP 0.1 nav. Rich Horigan, Director of 787 Systems at Boeing, told Aviation Tech Today that "the 787 can fly point-to-point to or from any runway without engaging ground navigation aids.".

    According to recent reports, the 787 is uniquely designed to cruise through a temporary loss of GPS signal of up to 20 minutes while maintaining RNP. The system enables airlines to fly RNP AR routes and allows pilots to fly precise curved paths around mountains, obstacles, or noise-sensitive areas. Because of its high accuracy, pilots can often fly to lower decision altitudes.

    #123616. When To Use The Flight Attendant Call Button (And When To Skip It)

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1485 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Onemileatatime ↗ Open Full Page

    When To Use The Flight Attendant Call Button (And When To Skip It)

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1485 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • To push the flight attendant call button, or not to push the flight attendant call button, that is the question.
    • In a recent development, every airplane seat has a flight attendant call button, typically in the overhead console, right by the reading light and individual air nozzle (if the plane has those).
    • Industry observers note that the flight attendant call button typically depicts a person with a tray, suggesting that the call button is intended for service.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    To push the flight attendant call button, or not to push the flight attendant call button, that is the question. I’ll share my take, and then I’m curious to hear how OMAAT readers feel. Let’s start with some background, and then we’ll discuss best practices….

    In a recent development, every airplane seat has a flight attendant call button, typically in the overhead console, right by the reading light and individual air nozzle (if the plane has those). The flight attendant call button, is, as the name suggests, a way to call a flight attendant to your seat.

    Industry observers note that the flight attendant call button typically depicts a person with a tray, suggesting that the call button is intended for service. However, that’s not how all flight attendants interpret it, so I want to talk about that in a bit more detail.

    In most of the world, the flight attendant call button seems to work as intended. It’s a useful way to call over a flight attendant, whether you want a drink refill, or there’s some sort of an emergency.

    However, in the United States I’ve heard several flight attendants over the years announce that the call button is in fact the “emergency flight attendant call button,” advising passengers to only use it if absolutely necessary. Suffice to say that this kind of announcement isn’t approved by any airline.

    While people will often joke “well I’m happy you consider my drink request to be an emergency,” let’s talk about when it’s actually appropriate to use a flight attendant call button.

    Broadly speaking, it’s always appropriate to use the flight attendant call button for service in first & business class, especially on international airlines. You’re paying a premium for more service, and having an extra request on a long haul flight isn’t unreasonable.

    In a recent development, I’ll take it a step further — at top airlines, crews generally prefer that you push the call button rather than going to the galley with your request. Foreign carriers typically have thick curtains between the galley and the cabin, and you generally shouldn’t try to go into the flight attendant’s “space” without permission. They’d much rather come to you. They might be putting on some makeup or eating a meal, and don’t want to be caught off guard. So absolutely push the flight attendant call button — it’s the courteous thing to do.

    It has been revealed that I do want to mention just one caveat — try to be respectful of the overall service flow. For example, if a cabin has 50+ business class seats and the crew is doing service with a cart and is currently in the aisle, wait until they finish that round of service before pushing the call button again, unless there’s something you absolutely need.

    When it comes to using the call button, you can’t beat Emirates first class, where you can voice or video call the crew with any requests, without them even having to come to your seat.

    It has been revealed that it’s also interesting to observe the cultural differences between airlines when it comes to service approaches. For example, in Singapore Airlines first class I generally don’t push the flight attendant call button, since even on a long haul flight, a crew member seems to pass through the cabin every 10-15 minutes throughout the flight. The service is just so proactive that I don’t find it necessary.

    Cathay Pacific first class is exactly the opposite — the crews are spectacularly reactive. That might sound sarcastic, but it’s not. On Cathay Pacific you (hopefully) won’t see a flight attendant once between meal services without calling them, and that’s so that your privacy is maximized. But if you push the call button a flight attendant will cheerily appear within seconds.

    Sources indicate that of course those are both airlines known for great service. You have all kinds of other airlines where flight attendants make a habit of not passing through the cabin, and when they do they almost seem to look down, to avoid making eye contact.

    It has been revealed that using the flight attendant call button in economy is trickier. There’s nothing inherently wrong with it, but the staffing ratio in economy is different than in first & business class, and in many cases flight attendants have to walk a lot further to your seat. Also keep in mind that on long haul flights the crew has rest periods, reducing the staffing ratio even further.

    Personally I think there’s nothing wrong with using the call button in economy:.

    Recent findings suggest that that being said, in economy I also think it’s more reasonable to stretch your legs and go to the galley yourself. Generally there’s a small setup with snacks and drinks, at least on long haul flights, so you can help yourself to that. Furthermore, in my experience flight attendants are typically “sitting in the open” more in economy than in business or first class, given that the volume of requests is greater.

    It has been revealed that the above are my general thoughts, though is the story any different on airlines in the United States? This accounts for the fact that:.

    On US airlines I’m generally a little more hesitant to use the call button. I see what kind of a vibe the crew gives me. In general I don’t mind pushing the call button in international first & business class on a US airline, while I avoid it on domestic flights. If I get the sense that the crew takes issue with use of the call button, I of course won’t use it.

    It has been revealed that all airplane seats have individual flight attendant call buttons, though customs around using them seem to differ. In the United States, some flight attendants seem to think these buttons are just for emergencies, while outside the United States there are consistently no complications with using them for service.

    Where do you stand on using the flight attendant call button, and what has your experience been?

    Us airline here . I’m more than happy to take call lights in any cabin. When it gets concerning is when I customs keeps pressing it for alcohol refills . I have never heard crew members making an announcement that the call light is for emergency only , except when customer press it during taxi, take off , and landing.

    Who else ran to the comments to see how you crazy folk use the call button.

    Recent findings suggest that I use it in business class if I'm done with a meal and am burried in the set table with plates and all. Without the call button the crew may not proactively come clear it for hours.

    According to recent reports, if the airline offered complementary drinks, then no reason not to use it to ask for another. Just because they served you one doesn’t make a difference, there’s no cap on how many drinks are complementary so it’s part of the job. If the tray hasn’t been cleared and you need the bathroom. Yes you should feel comfortable calling the crew. If you want your meal early, that’s pushing it. You want an extra blanket? Maybe. You want to adjust the cabin temperature; I’d reserve this request for premium cabins, unless the temperature is ridiculous. Merely my opinion though, of course, now how it practically works - you will always get some cabin crew who don’t want to do extra work so even resent basic aspects of their job like serving drinks or clearing a table so you can, you know, get out of your seat to the bathroom - not really optional! I’m too hot/cold, I can’t wait to eat? Well that’s getting ridiculous. Even as a frequent F traveller I don’t expect them to rush a fine meal service just because I’m impatient. In an F cabin with say 3 other passengers, changing the cabin temperature should be done gracefully and only pushed back if other customers are opposing the request. I can see how this will play out totally differently in a cabin with 100 other passengers in close proximity.

    I do not care what cabin I’m travelling in, I’m pressing the button if I want something.

    FCC pick advanced by Senate Commerce after Democratic boycott

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (898 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Ted Cruz, R-Texas, talks with reporters after the Senate luncheons in the Capitol on Tuesday.
    • The fight over partisan balance on the Federal Communications Commission snarled a Senate markup Wednesday morning as Republicans advanced a controversial nomination despite a Democratic boycott in an attempt to deny a quorum.
    • Republicans on the Commerce Committee voted unanimously to advance the nomination of Danielle Thumann Severs, a senior counsel to FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, to be a member of the commission, alongside several transportation and communications bills.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, talks with reporters after the Senate luncheons in the Capitol on Tuesday. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    The fight over partisan balance on the Federal Communications Commission snarled a Senate markup Wednesday morning as Republicans advanced a controversial nomination despite a Democratic boycott in an attempt to deny a quorum.

    Republicans on the Commerce Committee voted unanimously to advance the nomination of Danielle Thumann Severs, a senior counsel to FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, to be a member of the commission, alongside several transportation and communications bills.

    The fate of the nominations and bills could ultimately be decided via a challenge on the Senate floor, according to a Democratic committee staffer, speaking on condition of anonymity.

    In a statement Wednesday morning, committee Democrats, led by ranking member  Maria Cantwell of Washington, noted they objected to Thumann Severs’ nomination without a Democratic “pair” nomination and referenced a letter they sent to Chairman Ted Cruz, R-Texas, on Monday requesting the nomination be removed from the agenda.

    In a recent development, “Commissioner Anna Gomez could be re-nominated with all swiftness, as we have called for numerous times,” the group wrote. “This is not a problem we created, but a problem that the White House can solve.”.

    It has been revealed that thumann Severs, if confirmed, would give the FCC three Republican members and one Democrat, Gomez. The three Republicans could then constitute a quorum on the commission, allowing President Donald Trump to potentially fire Gomez. The commission generally has five members, three of the president’s party and two in the minority.

    Cruz stated at the markup that there is nothing in the law that requires moving nominees in pairs, and that committee Republicans would continue their work on what he called a nomination that followed a “typical process.”.

    Recent findings suggest that “Democrats will control the Senate, unfortunately, in January,” Cruz noted. “But today is November 18th. The American people elected each of us to fulfill our duties, including advice and consent, for our full terms.”.

    Related: Threats to broadcasters hang over FCC nominee hearing.

    The Democratic staffer told reporters that because the committee did not adopt rules at the beginning of the 119th Congress, it has been operating under rules from the 118th, which required the attendance of at least one member of the minority party to constitute a quorum for reporting bills or nominations.

    “The remaining recourse is to basically go to the floor and . . . make an inquiry in terms of what took place today, and then there would have to be a formal ruling by the chair,” they mentioned.

    They added that in determining whether the committee had a quorum to advance the nomination, “It would depend on how they view our committee rules from the 118th that we practice under for the 119th versus what the Senate rules are.” The staffer said they have not yet spoken with committee Democrats or Democratic leadership about plans for such an inquiry.

    In a recent development, democrats also previously boycotted a committee markup in March over an aviation safety bill left off the committee’s agenda, after which action was deferred. The committee later came to agreement and rescheduled the markup.

    In their letter Monday, Democrats quoted Cruz from a 2014 statement about the nomination of Loretta Lynch to be attorney general.

    “As you wrote in 2014, controversial nominees ‘should not be confirmed in the lame duck session of Congress by senators who just lost their seats and are no longer accountable to the voters.’ We agree,” the letter said.

    On Tuesday, Sen. Ben Ray Luján, D-N.M., wrote his own letter to Cruz calling for the removal of the nomination from the agenda based on grounds that Thumann Severs lied to the committee.

    “While Ms. Thumann testified she did not work ‘on any media-related complications,’ documents obtained through Freedom of Information Act requests demonstrate that she worked on several media related issues, including on commitments that Skydance made to pave the way for FCC approval of its merger with Paramount,” Luján wrote.

    Democrats have criticized the FCC and Carr for allowing media consolidation, including by Skydance. There has also been bipartisan criticism of Carr’s threats against broadcasters for speech he disagrees with.

    Luján told reporters Wednesday prior to the markup that he expects, under Democratic control next year, Carr and potentially Thumann Severs would be called to testify.

    “I have questions. I certainly hope that Brendan Carr will voluntarily show up to this committee when invited, and that other rules and tools do not need to be used,” Luján stated, responding to a question about possibly subpoenaing Carr. “But . . . everything should be on the table.”.

    According to recent reports, sen. Jerry Moran, R-Kan., mentioned at the markup that he spoke with Thumann Severs about her role at the FCC and her “lack of engagement” as the commission has made decisions regarding broadcasters. He also said he found her testimony at last week’s nomination hearing “comforting.”.

    “I have concerns with FCC action in regard to political speech, broadcasters, and she indicated in her answers . . . in a way that provided me with a level of comfort about her nomination in regard to that matter,” Moran said.

    Moran also said he hopes to meet with Thumann Severs before her nomination is brought to the floor.

    Chase Freedom Unlimited Review: No Annual Fee & 1.5x Points Everywhere
