    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Air India has made several changes to its network this year. The Indian flag carrier rolled out a three-weekly service between Mumbai and Toronto and plans to add Osaka Kansai to its international network next year.

    However, rising fuel prices and operational constraints stemming from the closure of Pakistani airspace have forced the airline to scale back parts of its network. At the same time, it has also transferred several routes (mostly domestic or short- to medium-haul) to its low-cost subsidiary, Air India Express.

    In a recent development, unsurprisingly, the list includes several European routes from Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport (DEL), which Simple Flying has previously reported on. These include the Star Alliance member’s services to Birmingham Airport (BHX), which ended earlier this month, Vienna International Airport (VIE) in Austria, and Copenhagen Airport (CPH) in Denmark.

    Recent findings suggest that some of the other international cuts are in the Middle East, mostly on routes to Dubai International Airport (DXB) and one to King Khalid International Airport (RUH) in Riyadh. Technically, many of these routes have not disappeared from the Air India Group's network. As shown in the table below, several are now operated by Air India Express.

    No direct connection to Delhi anymore.

    Removed Austria's only connection to India.

    Operated by Air India Express (4x weekly from December).

    Operated by Air India Express (2x daily).

    Complete withdrawal from Chennai's international market.

    Replaced by Air India Express (5x weekly).

    Replaced by Air India Express (up to 2x daily).

    Industry observers note that as for the domestic cuts, the Indian flag carrier has largely handed over these routes to its subsidiary. The Tata Group consolidated its four airlines into two in 2024, merging Vistara with Air India and AIX Connect with Air India Express. Under this structure, the Star Alliance member appears to be focusing more on its full-service operations.

    According to recent reports, meanwhile, it has been handing over several price-sensitive, point-to-point routes to its low-cost subsidiary. Air India Express has taken over the group's operations at several non-metro airports, including Aurangabad, Bhopal, Coimbatore, Jamnagar, Jodhpur, Madurai and Tirupati. The airline now serves 48 domestic and 16 international destinations.

    Yes (daily until the end of this month; restarting in April 2027).

    For the current winter season, according to schedule data from aviation analytics manufacturer Cirium, the low-cost carrier has scheduled 78,202 flights, up 5.1% from the 74,374 flights it offered last winter. It has more than 70 daily international flights on its schedule and offers up to 390 daily flights across its domestic network.

    According to recent reports, nevertheless, we have seen some interesting additions to Air India's international network this year. In May, the airline introduced five weekly flights between Delhi and Hanoi's Noi Bai International Airport (HAN) in Vietnam. The following month, it introduced four weekly flights between Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (BOM) and Tokyo Haneda International Airport (HND) using its Boeing 787-8s.

    Recent findings suggest that in addition, last month, it started a new winter seasonal service between Mumbai and Toronto Pearson International Airport (YYZ). From February 2, 2027, it will also operate four weekly flights between Delhi and Osaka's Kansai International Airport (KIX) using its Boeing 787-8s. It will become the only airline offering nonstop flights between India and Osaka.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • On September 30, 2026, we saw an unbelievably horrifying attempted terror plot, whereby a flydubai Boeing 737 first officer attempted to hijack the plane he was second in command of, and crash it into Tel Aviv’s Ben Gurion Airport.
    • Recent findings suggest that he attempted to kill the captain of the flight using the axe in the cockpit, but thank goodness the captain managed to open the door after being struck, so that passengers could restrain the first officer.
    • Ever since that incident, flydubai has been banned from flying to Israel.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    On September 30, 2026, we saw an unbelievably horrifying attempted terror plot, whereby a flydubai Boeing 737 first officer attempted to hijack the plane he was second in command of, and crash it into Tel Aviv’s Ben Gurion Airport.

    Recent findings suggest that he attempted to kill the captain of the flight using the axe in the cockpit, but thank goodness the captain managed to open the door after being struck, so that passengers could restrain the first officer. The details that have come out ever since have been downright chilling, including how the Omani pilot had specifically sought out a job at flydubai because the airline flew to Israel, and he wanted to crash into the airport there.

    Ever since that incident, flydubai has been banned from flying to Israel. For that matter, air service between Israel and the United Arab Emirates is just a tiny fraction of what it previously was. However, there’s now an patch, and it looks like this service could resume very soon.

    The Times of Israel reports that Israeli Transportation Minister Miri Regev has approved the resumption of flydubai flights to Israel, pending approval from Israel’s security authorities.

    This approval comes after a delegation of Israeli security and transportation officials traveled to Dubai to meet with their counterparts, to discuss fresh security measures to allow airlines to resume flights between Tel Aviv and Dubai.

    Emirati officials reportedly presented the Israeli officials with newly introduced steps that have been taken to ensure security in light of the incident, but details beyond that haven’t been made public. Per a statement from the Israeli Transportation Ministry:.

    “The delegation today presented Regev with the steps the company has taken in the wake of the incident. As a result, Regev approved the return of flydubai, subject to clearance from security authorities. The move is a significant step toward restoring air connectivity between Israel and the UAE and expanding flight options for passengers.”.

    It has been revealed that tel Aviv was flydubai’s single biggest destination, as the airline operated in the market with up to 10 daily flights. Previously, Israeli authorities had banned flydubai from returning to the country through at least December 15, 2026.

    Let's talk about that missing rudder of Flydubai 1073 B737 MAX 8.The aerodynamic forces involved may have been large enough to cause rudder failure through aerodynamic flutter during the extreme overspeed.The aircraft descended more than 14,000 ft in under 30 seconds.Even… pic.twitter.com/ECA34H4IXG.

    Israel is typically known for its very tight security and good intelligence, but obviously there are lapses sometimes.

    It has been revealed that one of the odd things about the flydubai attempted terror attack is that the Israeli government reportedly had a policy whereby pilots of foreign airlines couldn’t hold citizenship with countries that don’t have diplomatic relations with Israel. Oman and Israel don’t have diplomatic relations, so based on that, the first officer shouldn’t have been able to fly on the plane.

    Industry observers note that however, it sure seems that there wasn’t actually enforcement of this rule, given that the flydubai first officer had flown to Tel Aviv several times before. I’d imagine that Israeli forces will now much more closely screen the pilots on these flights.

    I am curious if there were some fresh policies put in place beyond that, or if the extent of the enforcement here is that it’s about the potential nationality of pilots.

    Israeli authorities have met with their counterparts in the UAE, and the strategy is for flydubai to be able to resume flights to Israel in the near future. This comes nearly two months after the awful terror plot, whereby a flydubai pilot intended to kill the captain, and then fly a 737 full of passengers into the terminal at Ben Gurion Airport.

    Some latest security policies have reportedly been put into place, though the details of that aren’t being made public. I think one thing is for sure — Israeli authorities will carefully be scrutinizing manifests and keeping an eye on the pilots at the controls of these flights.

    This resumption is a big deal for flydubai, given that Tel Aviv was the carrier’s biggest market.

    Tech Report: Tempers flare as future of Social Security debated

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Ron Johnson, R-Wis., said he wants to fix Social Security, while also calling it a "Ponzi scheme." (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).
    • If Congress ever tries to fix Social Security to address a looming shortfall, a Senate Budget Committee hearing Wednesday indicated how poisonous the politics could become.
    • Budget Chairman Ron Johnson, R-Wis., set the stage for a fierce partisan clash even before the hearing began by calling Social Security a "Ponzi scheme" in a Fox Business interview earlier in the day.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., said he wants to fix Social Security, while also calling it a "Ponzi scheme." (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    If Congress ever tries to fix Social Security to address a looming shortfall, a Senate Budget Committee hearing Wednesday indicated how poisonous the politics could become.

    Budget Chairman Ron Johnson, R-Wis., set the stage for a fierce partisan clash even before the hearing began by calling Social Security a "Ponzi scheme" in a Fox Business interview earlier in the day. Democrats erupted, accusing Johnson of scaring seniors and being unwilling to fix a financial lifeline for more than 72 million retirees.

    Sources indicate that “I think it’s outrageous,” mentioned Sen. Mark Warner, D-Va., one of several Democrats on the panel who slammed Johnson for his comments. “Don’t go out there scaring Americans to make political points on Fox News. This is too fricking vital.”.

    In a recent development, johnson acknowledged making an “imprecise comment” on prospects for a fix during the Fox interview. But he also told Democrats that if they had read his “chairman’s memo” he sent them Tuesday they would know he wants to preserve the system and pass a law to prevent any cuts to benefits if the Social Security Trust Fund is depleted.

    It has been revealed that "This is a scam, it’s grotesque, and at this point there’s really no way to fix Social Security," he said on Fox Business. "It’s a Ponzi scheme. You can’t fix it. You just shut it down and hope you can recover some of your money.”.

    But Johnson appeared to contradict himself later in the same interview, saying there is a difference with a “government-sanctioned Ponzi scheme” in that “you can force investors to keep putting money into it and that’s what we’ll probably have to do … You can fix Social Security and make it solvent.”.

    In his opening statement at the hearing, Johnson mentioned Congress should pass a law to prevent benefit cuts and then “roll up our sleeves and begin seriously addressing the main problem, our massive debt and deficits.” He said that is the only way to “ensure we have the financial wherewithal to honor promises made to seniors.”.

    In a recent development, johnson also told the panel he used the term “Ponzi scheme” in part to draw attention to the importance of addressing the problem. “If I gotta pay a political price for that, I really don’t care,” he said.

    Industry observers note that there is no doubt that a fix is needed. Without any change, Social Security recipients face a 22 percent cut in benefits by the end of 2032, according to projections from the Social Security Board of Trustees. Johnson mentioned Congress and the president won’t cut benefits even if the trust fund is exhausted.

    And there has been no shortage of Social Security bills introduced to provide a fix, but none of them has gained momentum.

    Industry observers note that sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, drew flak from fellow Republicans after he and Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., proposed lifting the cap on income subject to the Social Security payroll tax so that the tax would apply to all earned income.

    A bipartisan proposal, from Sens. Richard J. Durbin, D-Ill., Bill Cassidy, R-La., Tim Kaine, D-Va., and John Cornyn, R-Texas, would have put a plan in motion by requiring the Social Security Advisory Board to recommend a bill that would ensure Social Security is funded for at least the next 50 years.

    Senators on both sides of the aisle stated they were committed to fixing Social Security. Republicans stressed the importance of economic growth to bring in more revenue to the system and cautioned that tax increases would slow growth.

    Democrats pitched shifting more revenue into the system, for example by raising the cap on the payroll tax or taxing other income.

    “I do believe if we can be focused on fixing the Social Security stability problem, that could be a stepping stone to fixing broader problems,” noted Kaine, who is anticipated to chair the Budget Committee when Democrats take over Congress next year.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that one of the most interesting transatlantic flights will be returning yet again in 2027.
    • Recent findings suggest that in the summer of 2018, an interesting domestic transatlantic route rolled out — it operated seasonally once weekly.
    • Industry observers note that what’s Saint Pierre and Miquelon?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that one of the most interesting transatlantic flights will be returning yet again in 2027. Maybe this will be the year I finally get to try it, even if there’s no premium cabin angle!

    Recent findings suggest that in the summer of 2018, an interesting domestic transatlantic route rolled out — it operated seasonally once weekly. Specifically, ASL Airlines operated a Boeing 737-700 that was marketed by Air Saint-Pierre between Paris (CDG) and Saint Pierre and Miquelon (FSP).

    Industry observers note that what’s Saint Pierre and Miquelon? It’s a self-governing territory of France, situated in the northwestern Atlantic Ocean, near Newfoundland and Labrador. The islands cover an area of about 93 square miles, and have a population of just about 6,000 people.

    The territory’s airline, Air Saint-Pierre, only has turboprops, which the carrier flies to places like Halifax (YHZ), Montreal (YUL), and St. John’s (YYT). Obviously these planes aren’t capable of operating across the Atlantic, so the airline leases a Boeing 737 for the once weekly flight.

    Recent findings suggest that this was the first time ever that we saw a nonstop link between these territories and mainland France. There were some other things that made this route interesting:.

    Sources indicate that the route ended up returning in 2019, was then paused in 2020 and 2021 due to the pandemic, and then returned in 2022 through 2026. The route will now be returning yet again, for the 2027 season, so it sure seems like this is basically a permanent thing.

    The once weekly flight between Saint Pierre and Miquelon and Paris will be returning in 2027, between June 21 and September 6, 2027.

    According to recent reports, the route will once again be operated by an ASL Airlines France Boeing 737-700, and the flight will be marketed and sold by Air Saint-Pierre. The flight will operate westbound on Mondays and eastbound on Tuesdays, as follows:.

    Paris to Saint Pierre and Miquelon departing 4:00PM arriving 6:30PMSaint Pierre and Miquelon to Paris departing 10:30AM arriving 8:05PM.

    The 2,664-mile flight is blocked at 6hr30min westbound and 5hr35min eastbound. As you can see, the plane sits on the ground in Saint Pierre for quite a while. This is so that the crew can get their rest and operate the flight back the next day, rather than making them stay there for over a week.

    I imagine the airline is able to get a decent deal on parking at the airport for 16 hours. 😉 It’s also interesting since this is an eastbound daytime transatlantic flight, which is fairly rare.

    If you want to book a seat on this flight, below is the pricing for travel in both directions, with fares starting at €660 one-way for standard adult fares.

    It has been revealed that as you can see, the fare difference just comes down to the age of the traveler, as well as the level of flexibility you’d like, with fares either being non-refundable and non-changeable, non-refundable but changeable for a fee, or refundable and changeable. The plane is in an all-economy configuration, as there’s no premium cabin.

    Sources indicate that air Saint-Pierre will be bringing back its flight between Saint Pierre and Paris in the summer of 2027, operated by ASL Airlines. This is an absolutely fascinating route, and it’s so cool to see that it was launched in the first place, and is sticking around.

    According to recent reports, while the link between Paris and this French territory is obvious, it’s still kind of awesome that such a small territory can support a flight like this. But I guess the downside was fairly limited, since the route was subsidized from the beginning. Personally I find this to be the most intriguing transatlantic route.

    Anyone else love this Air Saint-Pierre flight as much as I do?

    Just 4 Years After Launch, This Airline’s Finances Are Now “Critical”

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, when Norse Atlantic Airways commenced operations four years ago, in June 2022, a upcoming dawn for transatlantic travel appeared to have arrived.
    • Sources indicate that this morning, Norse issued a statement about its financial situation and the strategic review it is undertaking as it looks to return to more stable economic ground.
    • Norse did not mince its words in Wednesday's statement, explaining outright that "the organization’s financial situation is critical" and "dependent on securing financing to meet its short-term liquidity needs and to continue its operations." Given the carrier's well-documented financial struggles, Norse is exploring various options for its future.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, when Norse Atlantic Airways commenced operations four years ago, in June 2022, a upcoming dawn for transatlantic travel appeared to have arrived. The carrier promised low-cost long-haul flights using a modern fleet of Boeing 787 Dreamliners, operating from Oslo Gardermoen Airport (OSL) in Norway and, via its UK division, Gatwick Airport (LGW) in London. Now, however, the airline is on the brink.

    Sources indicate that this morning, Norse issued a statement about its financial situation and the strategic review it is undertaking as it looks to return to more stable economic ground. The carrier described its financial footing as 'critical' and underlined the need to secure financing to remain operationally viable.

    Norse did not mince its words in Wednesday's statement, explaining outright that "the organization’s financial situation is critical" and "dependent on securing financing to meet its short-term liquidity needs and to continue its operations." Given the carrier's well-documented financial struggles, Norse is exploring various options for its future.

    In a recent development, in this regard, the airline explained on Wednesday morning that it continues to "entertain discussions for a potential takeover." Elsewhere, other options include placing greater emphasis on ACMI (wet lease) contractsto make up for its financial shortfall. The news will concern the airline's flyers and staff, and it has committed to "providing further information as and when appropriate." The airline also remarked it is in "discussions" with agencies to help with its finances.

    It has been revealed that "Norse is also engaged in discussions with selected parties on short-term financing. However, there can be no assurances that such discussions will result in a viable solution.".

    Industry observers note that when Norse commenced operations back in June 2022, its first route linked Oslo with John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) in New York City. Certain flights on this route operated via London, giving passengers flying between the UK and Norway the rare chance to fly short-haul on a 787. Norse then set up a UK subsidiary, allowing it to serve London without the Norway leg.

    Industry observers note that today, Asian leisure destinations also play an crucial role in Norse's winter network. According to Cirium, an aviation analytics company, Norse itself is operating scheduled flights from Oslo and Stockholm to Bangkok and Phuket in Thailand this month. Norse UK is operating flights from London Gatwick to Bangkok and Cape Town, with Orlando being its only US destination.

    Recent findings suggest that fleet-wise, data from ch-aviation highlights that Norse right now has a total of 12 787-9s. Of these, seven are registered in Norway, and five are registered in the UK. Interestingly, three of Norse Atlantic's five UK-registered Boeing 787s are already being used on ACMI contracts, with Pakistan International Airlines listed as their wet-lease customer.

    The fact that Norse has described its financial situation as critical casts serious doubt on the long-term economic viability of its operations. Unfortunately, the low-cost long-haul market is a difficult nut to crack, as has been proven time and again over the years. Another notable example of a failure on this front involved Norwegian Air Shuttle and its 787s.

    These Dreamliners operated low-cost intercontinental flights using both Boeing 787-8s (Norwegian Long Haul) and 787-9s (Norwegian Long-Haul and Norwegian Air UK). Much like Norse Atlantic, the carrier promised big things when it came to revolutionizing the long-haul scene for budget-conscious flyers. Unfortunately, the onset of the coronavirus pandemic brought these aims screeching to a sudden halt.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Southwest Airlines has several co-branded credit cards with Chase.
    • In a recent development, this is my in-depth Southwest Priority Card review, covering the card’s benefits.
    • Link: Learn more about the Southwest Rapid Rewards® Priority Credit Card.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Southwest Airlines has several co-branded credit cards with Chase. Of the three personal cards, my favorite one is the Southwest Rapid Rewards® Priority Credit Card.

    In a recent development, this is my in-depth Southwest Priority Card review, covering the card’s benefits. I’ll also explain how despite this being the highest annual fee personal card in the portfolio, I still think it represents the best deal. Now is also a good time to consider applying for the card if you’re a fan of Southwest’s popular Companion Pass perk.

    Link: Learn more about the Southwest Rapid Rewards® Priority Credit Card.

    Before I review the Southwest Priority Card benefits in detail, here’s a high-level look at everything you need to know about the card:.

    Here are my thoughts on the Southwest Priority Card’s main pros and cons:.

    If you’re thinking about applying for the Southwest Priority Card, you’re probably most interested in the welcome bonus it’s at the moment offering, along with its annual fee and general eligibility rules for getting the card. So let’s dive into those. I’ll also explain a recent change to how Southwest cards factor into qualifying for the Companion Pass, which pertains to all cards, not just the Priority.

    Industry observers note that the Southwest Priority Card is offering a limited time welcome bonus: Earn 90,000 bonus points after spending $3,000 on purchases in the first 3 months from account opening. This is higher than the standard welcome offer for the card, and its minimum spending requirement should be easy for most spenders to meet.

    In a recent development, rapid Rewards is a revenue-based frequent flyer program, and based on my latest miles & points valuations, I consider Rapid Rewards points to be worth 1.2 cents each. So, to me, the points from this welcome offer are worth $1,080.

    Chase and Southwest have some pretty strict rules when it comes to who is eligible for the card. The Southwest Priority Pass is not available to anyone who currently has a Southwest Rapid Rewards personal card, or anyone who has received a welcome bonus on a Southwest Rapid Rewards personal card in the past 24 months. However, you are eligible if you have a Southwest business credit card.

    Sources indicate that this is in addition to Chase’s general application rules, including the 5/24 rule, whereby you typically won’t be approved for a Chase card if you’ve opened five or more newly introduced card accounts in the past 24 months. However, that’s not enforced consistently.

    Recent findings suggest that when it comes to credit scores, there’s not a consistent score that you need to get approved for the card, though I’d hope to have a score in the “excellent” range. That being mentioned, people with lower scores have been approved, and people with higher scores have been rejected, as it’s one of only many factors that determines card eligibility.

    Industry observers note that the Southwest Priority Card has a $229 annual fee. As a point of comparison, the other personal cards have annual fees of $99 and $149, so the annual fee on this card is a bit higher. However, as I’ll explain below, the benefits could justify the premium annual fee.

    The card also has no extra cost to add authorized people, so you can add those for $0 each, so that authorized user spending can help you rack up rewards.

    The Southwest Priority Card has no foreign transaction fees, so this could be a useful card for your spending abroad. This is a Visa as well, and Visas are accepted pretty widely around the globe.

    Another rule worth mentioning here involves how Southwest credit card welcome bonuses help you earn the Companion Pass, which lets you bring a companion with you on flights (both cash and award tickets) and pay just taxes and fees.

    It has been revealed that for a long time now, the points earned as part of Southwest credit card welcome bonuses have counted towards the 135,000 qualifying points needed to earn the Companion Pass. But starting soon, credit card welcome bonuses will no longer count toward qualification.

    You’ll need to apply for a card by December 2, 2026, for your welcome bonus to count toward the Companion Pass for a final time. So apply for the Priority Card sooner rather than later if you’re hoping to earn that perk with the help of credit card spending.

    Now is also your last chance to get an annual boost of 10,000 Companion Pass qualifying points as a Southwest credit card holder. Starting next year, instead of a boost of 10,000 TQPs for having a Southwest card, you’ll get 10,000 TQPs if your TQP balance is 130,000 by December 31, 2027. That would be enough to get you to Platinum status, which will include unlimited Companion Pass trips as a benefit.

    This change eliminates the easiest way to earn this valuable benefit, and it’s not the only upcoming rule: referral bonuses, anniversary points, bonus points from spending, and partner spending won’t count toward the Companion Pass either. In fact, Southwest’s rolling the Companion Pass into its highest elite tier, Platinum, and requiring either 140,000 TQPs or 100 qualifying flights to earn it.

    Beyond the Southwest Priority Card airline benefits, a major draw is the card’s points earning on every purchase you make — plus how it can help you work toward Southwest elite status through earning Tier Qualifying Points.

    The Southwest Priority Card offers the following points for credit card spending:.

    Industry observers note that personally, I’d generally only put spending on the card if you’re going for A-List status and/or Companion Pass, because there are better cards for everyday spending otherwise. But still, those are some fairly solid bonus categories.

    As part of an overhaul of the Rapid Rewards program, Southwest is simplifying TQP earning on credit cards. Starting in 2027, every dollar spent on a co-branded Southwest credit card will earn you one TQP. In other words, $35K in spending would earn you Silver, $65K in spending would earn you Gold, and $140K in spending would earn you Platinum.

    This earning rate is the same across cards, so this isn’t specific to the Southwest Priority Card.

    I have a dedicated post that covers how to redeem Southwest Rapid Rewards points for maximum value, but let’s briefly look at how you can use the points you earn from the Southwest Priority Card.

    Industry observers note that rapid Rewards is a revenue-based frequent flyer program, meaning that the value you get from your points is tied to the cash cost of Southwest tickets. There are a few different levels, ranging from Basic tickets to Choice Extra fares, so the exact value can vary a bit.

    Basic award fares tend to offer the best redemption value. You’ll also usually get the best value on international Southwest routes to destinations like Costa Rica and Aruba. I’ve been able to get about 2.0 cents per point on these redemptions.

    It has been revealed that starting in spring 2027, Southwest will add points earning and redemption opportunities with select airline partners, which should make your Rapid Rewards points more valuable for international travel. The planned partners include Icelandair, China Airlines, and Etihad Airways — I look forward to seeing how these add value to the program.

    One great thing about the Southwest Rapid Rewards program is that there are no change or cancellation fees, and rebooking a fare when the price drops gets you a refund equal to any difference in points. Just note that Basic fares can only be changed by upgrading to a higher fare bundle, so for a cheaper Basic award you’d cancel and rebook rather than change.

    Sources indicate that as Southwest’s highest annual fee personal credit card, the Southwest Priority Card has the most benefits, including several that can improve your travel experience with the airline. Here are the card’s most notable ongoing perks.

    Southwest Priority Card holders can select a Preferred seat on Southwest at the time of booking for no extra charge. If Preferred seats aren’t available on your flight, you should be able to select a standard seat for free. Preferred seats are located near the front of the cabin, so having one usually means you’ll board and deplane faster.

    In a recent development, preferred seats generally cost about $30 to $60 extra, and selecting free Preferred seats at booking is a perk of Southwest Silver elite status. If you don’t have status and you’re able to use this benefit, you could get real value even after just a few Southwest flights.

    The Southwest Priority Card also offers unlimited upgrades to extra legroom seats within 48 hours prior to departure. This perk applies to the main cardholder as well as up to eight additional passengers on the same reservation.

    Extra legroom seat prices vary by route, but they generally cost roughly $40 to $100. On a route where they’re at the higher end of this range and you have multiple companions on your reservation, you could even recoup the Priority Card’s annual fee through one trip alone.

    Sources indicate that keep in mind that complimentary extra legroom seats within 48 hours of departure is another benefit of Southwest Silver status. So if you have that level of status or higher already, you don’t need the Priority Card to enjoy this perk.

    The Southwest Priority Card gets the primary cardholder and up to eight additional passengers on the same reservation a first checked bag at no additional cost. Checked bags on Southwest cost $45 each way, so this can save you up to $90 roundtrip on checked bag fees per person.

    With even a couple of roundtrip flights per year, this benefit can offset the annual fee — and about five one-way checked bags per year could cover it as well.

    With the Southwest Priority Card, you’ll be able to board with Group 5, or earlier if you have elite status or a fare or seat type that qualifies you for an earlier boarding group.

    According to recent reports, southwest has eight total boarding groups, so while there are several ahead of Group 5, it’s better than boarding last. This benefit applies to the main cardholder and up to eight passengers on the same reservation.

    Sources indicate that on your Southwest Priority Card anniversary every year, you’ll receive 7,500 bonus Rapid Rewards points. Southwest Rapid Rewards is a revenue-based frequent flyer program, and you can generally expect that you’ll need around 83 Rapid Rewards points for every dollar of airfare you book.

    In a recent development, in other words, 7,500 bonus points get you around $90 in Southwest airfare annually. That covers more than a third of the annual fee right there.

    Recent findings suggest that if you pay with your Southwest Priority Card you can save 25% on inflight Wi-Fi and drink purchases. You’ll receive statement credits for the 25% within two billing cycles of your purchase (though usually much faster than that).

    The Southwest Priority Card offers a variety of travel & purchase protection benefits, including:.

    Of course, you’ll want to check the cardmember agreement for the full terms & conditions associated with these benefits.

    Even though the Southwest Priority Card has the highest annual fee of any personal Chase Southwest card, it might be worthy of consideration.

    Sources indicate that many people love flying Southwest for the ability to earn the Southwest Companion Pass, the lack of change fees and vouchers that don’t expire. For others, Southwest is just a practical airline to fly on occasion, given its massive route network. Regardless, there’s lots of value in having points and benefits on Southwest.

    In a recent development, that said, not everyone needs a Southwest credit card — and even among Southwest credit cards, there’s a cheaper option that could make more sense if you only fly the airline a few times a year. Let’s look at some alternatives and how they stack up.

    Industry observers note that first, here’s a look at how the Southwest Priority Card compares to the other two personal Southwest cards. Note that all three cards have the free checked bag benefit and Group 5 boarding, so I left that out of the comparison table here.

    According to recent reports, the Southwest Rapid Rewards® Premier Credit Card (learn more) is one step down from the Southwest Priority Card, with a $149 annual fee and slightly pared-down perks. If you care about getting complimentary Preferred seat selection at the time of booking, the Priority Card is a better pick, since the Premier Card only offers this within 48 hours of departure.

    Other differences between the Priority and Premier cards include:.

    The Southwest Premier Card could be a decent alternative if you want a lower annual fee and don’t care about the lower earning rate on Southwest and caps on the other bonus categories.

    It has been revealed that there’s also the Southwest Rapid Rewards® Plus Credit Card (learn more). This is the entry-level personal Southwest credit card, with a $99 annual fee. As you’d expect, it has the fewest benefits among the personal Southwest cards. Here’s a quick breakdown:.

    I think the Southwest Priority Card provides significantly more value than the Southwest Plus Card, so the higher annual fee could still be worth it.

    If you’re looking to complement your Southwest Priority Card with a Southwest business card, consider the incredible Southwest® Rapid Rewards® Performance Business Credit Card (learn more). This card has some nice perks, including:.

    In a recent development, chase Ultimate Rewards is a transfer partner with Southwest Rapid Rewards, and points transfer at a 1:1 ratio. As a general rule of thumb, you’re going to earn points at a faster rate through Ultimate Rewards than through Rapid Rewards, not to mention that your points have a lot more flexibility.

    Should you earn Rapid Rewards points directly with a Southwest card, or with a Chase Ultimate Rewards card?

    For context, some of the best cards for earning Chase Ultimate Rewards points include the following:.

    On top of that, the following four no annual fee cards earn points that can be converted into Ultimate Rewards points at a 1:1 ratio in conjunction with one of the above cards:.

    When providing credit card advice, my answer to whether or not it makes sense to get a certain card is usually “it depends.” and this is the case as well with the Southwest Priority Card, especially given the latest changes to the Southwest Rapid Rewards program.

    Why I’ll Never Fly Ryanair, Even If It’s The Only Option

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (934 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that love them or hate them, low-cost airlines dominate the skies in some parts of the world.
    • Back in my late teens and early 20s, I was all for booking the cheapest ticket to a place I’d never heard of, just because I could.
    • That said, I still do still love to find a bargain, and can spend hours researching the best value option even when booking the simplest of itineraries.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that love them or hate them, low-cost airlines dominate the skies in some parts of the world. Nowhere is that more true than in Europe, home to Ryanair, the largest low-cost airline in the world (per 2025 passenger numbers).

    Back in my late teens and early 20s, I was all for booking the cheapest ticket to a place I’d never heard of, just because I could.

    That said, I still do still love to find a bargain, and can spend hours researching the best value option even when booking the simplest of itineraries. The buck stops, however, at Ryanair. My last flight was in 2023, and despite nothing glaringly awful happening, I vowed it would be the last.

    According to recent reports, part of the low-cost airline business model is choosing airports far from the cities they serve, since landing fees are often cheaper. One of the best examples of this is Frankfurt Hahn (HHN), located about 80 miles from Frankfurt am Main — the city the airport’s named after.

    Industry observers note that after a quick check on the Uber app, a one-way Uber ride would likely cost around $180. A more wallet-friendly alternative would be this €24 bus. The journey time would likely be longer than the flight itself….

    Even Ryanair’s largest base at London Stansted (STN) is around 40 miles from London, and requires a relatively expensive train or lengthy bus journey to the city.

    This is the part I hate the most about Ryanair. They are so stingy that they built their planes with built-in steps at the front boarding door so they don’t have to pay for air bridges. Whether it’s a sizzling 110+ degrees in the middle of the day in Seville, or deep in the minuses at Rovaniemi in Finland (the gateway to Lapland and Ryanair’s northernmost airport), you’ll have to brace the elements while boarding and deplaning.

    Industry observers note that getting a deal on a flight departing at daft o’clock in the morning isn’t limited to just Ryanair or low-cost airlines. Who would ever want to set an alarm before 6 a.m.? However, Ryanair can charge such a premium to fly at a respectable time of day, that its fares end up almost the same as flag carriers.

    According to recent reports, the screenshot below is a great example. British Airways’ one-way fares of 88 pounds from Heathrow (LHR) are over twice as much as two of Ryanair’s options from Stansted to Berlin.

    However, Ryanair charges £74 for its midday departure (without a cabin bag). Compare that to BA’s 1:20 p.m. departure for £88 including a cabin bag; it’s a wonder why anyone would even consider Ryanair’s option if they needed to fly in the middle of the day.

    Ultimately, airline preference is very subjective, and I know there are some die-hard Ryanair fans who won’t hear a bad word said about the airline. In its defense, if you’re heading somewhere off the beaten track, you can usually rely on Ryanair to get you as close as possible.

    Personally, I’d rather enjoy status benefits (and earn miles and status-earning points) by flying a legacy carrier like Air France-KLM, British Airways, or Lufthansa to the closest airport, then figure out ground transportation the rest of the way.

    Where do you stand on flying Ryanair?

    #123579. Latest Update: I Flew A United Airlines Boeing 737 MAX From A Remote Island Airport With Just 2 Weekly Flights: Here's What It Was Like

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1545 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Simpleflying ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: I Flew A United Airlines Boeing 737 MAX From A Remote Island Airport With Just 2 Weekly Flights: Here's What It Was Like

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1545 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that from its regional hub in Guam, United Airlines is the only airline that provides regular air connections to some of the small Micronesian islands in the Pacific.
    • One of the most notable regional flight connections United offers is the famous Island Hopper, which flies from Guam to Chuuk, Pohnpei, Kosrae, Kwajalein, Majuro, and Honolulu, and back again.
    • Recent findings suggest that describing island hopping in Micronesia with United is often much more about the experience at the airport than with United itself.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that from its regional hub in Guam, United Airlines is the only airline that provides regular air connections to some of the small Micronesian islands in the Pacific. Flying on some of these routes is a memorable experience, with local airports operating a TSA- and FAA-compliant system on sleepy little islands. Some island airports only wake up for a flight every second day. In November 2026, I flew from the island of Yap (a state in the Federated States of Micronesia or FSM) to Guam on board a United flight.

    One of the most notable regional flight connections United offers is the famous Island Hopper, which flies from Guam to Chuuk, Pohnpei, Kosrae, Kwajalein, Majuro, and Honolulu, and back again. I wanted to take this flight to Majuro, but it was beyond my budget. Some United Micronesia flights operate only twice a week, meaning the flight schedule dictates the tour schedule. On the upside, many of these Micronesian flights routinely operate half-full, meaning booking out is unusual for certain routes.

    Recent findings suggest that describing island hopping in Micronesia with United is often much more about the experience at the airport than with United itself. Yap International Airport is served only by United flights (with 737s) twice a week from Guam and by Pacific Missionary Aviation's (PMA) Beechcraft Super King Air 200 flights (with seven to nine passengers) once a week from Palau. PMA is set to introduce a second weekly flight next year.

    It has been revealed that as these are Yap's only regularly scheduled passenger flights, the airport is generally otherwise closed. I flew from Palau to Yap with PMA and then to Guam with United Airlines. As explained below, PMA offers the only scheduled passenger access to Yap for those who cannot pass through US immigration.

    Sources indicate that there are no direct flights connecting the State of Yap with the three other far-flung states of Chuuk, Pohnpei, and Kosrae​​​​​. To access those other islands and avoid United (and US immigration), the main alternative is Nauru Airlines. United's flight from Yap to Guam departs at 2:30 am, arriving in Guam at around 4:00 am, making it difficult to decide whether to book a hotel for the night before, the night of, or not at all. I opted not to book.

    It has been revealed that the experience of checking into United's various island flights differs significantly by island and airport. Some airports (especially on Saipan) are much larger and more sophisticated than Yap, but Yap was the one I flew through, and so I will describe that one here. Yap's check-in and baggage drop-off facilities are located in a covered area outside the building. During the check-in process, there is no air conditioning.

    Sources indicate that at the baggage drop-off (positioned before check-in), the staff informed me that their equipment was broken, so my bag would be manually searched. Many of the bags being checked in for the flight were wares in basic boxes and containers by locals to sell on other islands. Check-in was straightforward, with me presenting my current passport and my expired passport with the US visa.

    One of the notable features of Yap is that the country does not collect the exit fee in the airfare. There is a window where passengers must pay the $20 exit fee before going to the adjacent immigration window. These two windows are located on the outside of the airport. After stamping the passport out of the country, there is nothing in principle to stop passengers from walking away into the night, away from the airport. Passengers wait outside the airport until the security check opens.

    It has been revealed that even though the United flight was at most half full, perhaps a third, the entire check-in and security process was rather slow. This was particularly true of the security check. It appeared that the TSA had a representative at the station to oversee the security check, although I didn't ask, and I'm unsure. Security was one of the slowest I've seen in the world, perhaps the slowest.

    Only after the security check do passengers move into the airport's only waiting room with the sole boarding gate. Located outside the airport terminal is a very basic shop selling some snacks; inside the airport terminal, there is none. The turnaround time for United flights is slow compared with main airports. The Boeing 737 MAX 8 touches down at 1:10 AM and departs at 2:35 AM.

    Yap Airport lacks a Passenger Boarding Bridge (PBB) and a shuttle bus. Passengers walk from the terminal to the aircraft parked on the apron. The flight was perhaps around a third booked. I asked the local passenger next to me, and he remarked the flight is typically half empty. That United flight is the primary connection for Yapese, whose population is made up of around 7,000 people on the main island and 4,000 on the outer islands.

    Industry observers note that being a modern international US airport, Guam International Airport is dramatically different from Yap. One of the most notable features of the airport is its lack of a transit area, requiring all connecting passengers to pass through US immigration. I was visiting Guam for two days, so I planned to go through immigration anyway. Due to my travel record (which includes Iran, Somalia, Pakistan, among other countries), I was questioned by CBP for three hours.

    While Guam is not a particularly large airport, it is large enough to feel like a large international airport, especially after visiting remote Pacific airports. Renting cars is straightforward and easy, with my rental only requiring a $100 security deposit and not requiring a credit card. From Guam, passengers can island hop with United to Palau, the Northern Mariana Islands, the FSM, the Marshall Islands, Hawaii, and various other mainstream destinations (e.g., Japan, Taiwan).

    United Airlines' Island Hopper Destinations (per United).

    Non-Island Hopper Micronesian routes.

    Saipan (Northern Mariana Islands).

    According to recent reports, united is the only mainline US airline operating at Guam with a near-monopoly (99%) on local, regional, and US routes. According to the airport's report, United operated 87 weekly flights to 14 destinations over the greater region in 2024. The airport is also served by a number of Asian international carriers, including Japan Airlines, Korean Air, Jin Air, Philippine Airlines, and Air Busan. I flew out on Philippine Airlines.

    I flew on a newly introduced United Boeing MAX 8 (registered N37319) that was delivered in 2023. The airliner is at the moment tasked with island-hopping routes in the region, including the Island Hopper itself. Other recent destinations include Osaka, Tokyo, and Manila. No food or refreshments are served on the Yap to Guam flight, whose flight time is around one hour and ten minutes. The lack of refreshments is perhaps welcome, as that hour was the only time I got all night to close my eyes.

    While the flight is technically an international flight, in terms of aircraft allocation and configuration, United treats it as a domestic flight. The MAX 8 is configured in a two-class layout. It is fitted with 16 United First (domestic business class) seats and 150 economy class seats (including Economy Plus) for a total of 166 seats. The seats are comfortable for economy. Overall, United's economy class seems to be roughly equivalent to some higher-end, low-cost Asian carriers like AirAsia.

    Industry observers note that there is in-seat entertainment as well as in-seat charging (USB and power outlets). Perhaps due to the low capacity and the lack of competition, United's fares to Micronesian islands are typically expensive, with hops between islands often costing more than flights to destinations in Asia. As United has a monopoly in some cases, there is little choice but to accept the fares.

    In a recent development, united Airlines dominates the international and main route connections of the island nations of Palau, the Federated States of Micronesia, and the Marshall Islands, along with the US territories of Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands. This is largely a legacy of the American administration of the former Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands (TTPI) that it inherited after WWII, having conquered the islands from Japan. Eventually, the TTPI broke up and became three independent nation-states and the US Northern Mariana Commonwealth.

    United is effectively the commercial successor to Air Micronesia. Air Micronesia was set up in 1968 by Continental Airlines, Aloha Airlines, and the United Micronesian Development Association. It connected the various main islands with Guam and other regional destinations. For the region, this was a major development as the islands previously lacked a viable alternative. Later on, the airline was rebranded as Continental Micronesia with Guam as its main operating hub. In time, the Trust Territory broke up, but none of the succeeding countries was large enough to sustain its own national airline providing higher-end air services.

    The volume of passenger traffic is also small, leading to United flights often flying partially empty, meaning there is little scope to accommodate two competing airlines. In 2010, United Airlines merged with Continental Airlines, with the two integrating their operations. In 2017, the legacy Continental Micronesia separate operating certificate was retired, leaving the core United brand alone.

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1062 w)

    New FAA Rule For Planes Lining Up On Runways May Cause Delays

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1062 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has just added some upcoming restrictions to how air traffic controllers can clear aircraft to “line up and wait” on the runway, in anticipation of takeoff clearance.
    • According to recent reports, as of today (November 24, 2026), the FAA has introduced a upcoming rule regarding how aircraft can be cleared onto runways at airports.
    • In a recent development, to give an example, sometimes a plane will be cleared for takeoff, and then a bit of separation is required until the next plane can depart.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has just added some upcoming restrictions to how air traffic controllers can clear aircraft to “line up and wait” on the runway, in anticipation of takeoff clearance. This is intended to add an extra safety buffer, but to quote an airline pilot on an ATC frequency, “that’s probably going to cause some delays, that’s for sure.”.

    According to recent reports, as of today (November 24, 2026), the FAA has introduced a upcoming rule regarding how aircraft can be cleared onto runways at airports. Air traffic controllers want to utilize runways as efficiently as possible for both takeoffs and landings, and that often involves having planes line up on the runway and wait, in anticipation of takeoff clearance.

    In a recent development, to give an example, sometimes a plane will be cleared for takeoff, and then a bit of separation is required until the next plane can depart. In those situations, it’s common for the air traffic controller to clear that next plane to “line up and wait.”.

    The idea is that the plane then has clearance to enter the runway, and then await further takeoff clearance. After all, it might take 30 seconds or so for a plane to taxi from the hold short point of the runway, to getting into position on the runway.

    Under the new FAA rules, air traffic controllers will only be allowed to clear pilots to “line up and wait” in situations where there’s a dedicated supervisor or controller-in-charge who can’t perform other duties while these operations are underway. In the past this was a recommendation, but now this is a rule.

    Given constant air traffic control staffing shortages, this could actually impact operations a good percentage of the time. Here’s how the reason for this policy change is described:.

    Sources indicate that the core purpose of this change is to elevate the safety standard for Line Up and Wait (LUAW) operations by removing ambiguity in staffing requirements. By upgrading the guidance from “should” (a recommendation) to “must” (a mandatory requirement), the FAA ensures that the personnel providing watch supervision (OS/CIC) are fully dedicated to overseeing the safety of the operation without the distraction of simultaneously managing other operational tasks.

    It has been revealed that I can appreciate the concept behind this, which is to improve safety. After all, we have air traffic controllers who are spread too thin, and all too often, they get a bit distracted due to the volume of things they have to deal with. That has definitely been a contributing factor to many accidents and incidents over the years.

    Sources indicate that I do find the timing of this being introduced to be interesting, as it comes during one of the busiest travel periods of the year. I don’t think this will actually lead to any major issues, and for that matter, safety shouldn’t be compromised just because flights are busy.

    If you’re an observant passenger who is always looking out the window and is on Flightradar24, you may notice this policy in practice, for situations where you feel like the plane should already be lining up on the runway, but isn’t.

    According to recent reports, I can’t imagine this policy change will lead to any major delays on a widespread basis, but then again, given how at capacity many airports are, even a little change can make a big difference. Below you can hear some talk between an air traffic controller at Albuquerque Airport (ABQ) and a Southwest pilot, where they’re discussing the change. As you can hear, the pilot states “that’s probably going to cause some delays, that’s for sure.”.

    A new FAA runway safety requirement takes effect across the United States tomorrow, November 24, and an air traffic controller in Albuquerque is already warning pilots about possible delays.The change requires airports to have a dedicated supervisor on duty before controllers… pic.twitter.com/zxXariHNAy.

    While the FAA is making changes intended to improve safety, how about also requiring air traffic controllers in the United States to start using standard phraseology, like everywhere else in the world? 😉.

    Industry observers note that as of today, the FAA has added a fresh restriction on planes being able to line up on runways. A “line up and wait” procedure is pretty standard, but will now only be allowed in situations where the air traffic controller is only focused on one thing. Given how short staffed air traffic control often is, this could have some implications.

    I don’t think this will meaningfully slow things down on a national level, but for airports that make the most of every second to get planes in and out, it could definitely have implications.

    What do you make of the FAA’s upcoming restrictions on takeoff?

    It has been revealed that bermudAir, the unusual boutique carrier that debuted operations a few years back, keeps getting stranger. The company has just confirmed a massive expansion for the summer of 2027, and with this, we’ll see the airline add all kinds of seemingly random routes to and from Bermuda, plus all kinds of routes that don’t touch Bermuda.

    Whether you want to fly from Nashville to Ocho Rios, or from Fredericton to Bermuda, the airline now has you covered!

    It has been revealed that for a little bit of background, in mid-2023 we saw the launch of BermudAir, a quirky niche airline with the goal of operating Embraer jets between Bermuda (BDA) and the United States and Canada. Initially the airline was going to operate all-business class planes, but it scrapped (“delayed”) that concept before launch, instead introducing a two-cabin concept (though business class just has blocked adjacent seats and better service).

    As I mentioned from the beginning, the whole thing struck me as an odd venture, essentially trying to serve Bermuda year-round profitably, while going up against the major carriers that serve the airport.

    Sources indicate that to my surprise, the airline is still in business over three years after launch, though it hasn’t necessarily been that smooth. As is pretty common for an airlines startup, the first years have been rocky, with several routes being cut after launch. For that matter, the airline faced a lawsuit over millions in unpaid airport fees at its hub, which isn’t exactly a great sign.

    Several months back, BermudAir announced new winter 2026-2027 seasonal flying to places other than Bermuda. Now the airline has announced summer seasonal flying for 2027, and it’s arguably even stranger. The routes are all over the place.

    In the summer of 2027, BermudAir will fly from Bermuda (BDA) to the following destinations:.

    On top of that, the airline will be expanding beyond Bermuda, with latest seasonal services in the following markets:.

    Below is BermudAir’s updated map with destinations listed….

    Recent findings suggest that I really can’t make sense of what is going on at BermudAir. I feel like we’ve had reasons to be suspicious, when you look at the initial business model, vs. how things have played out:.

    I’m not suggesting there’s no demand in any of these upcoming markets. The demand may very well be there. But there are a lot of challenges here:.

    Sources indicate that what’s interesting here is how the airline unveiled seems to be taking a similar strategy both for this winter and for next summer. So based on the fact that the airline is moving forward with its current winter schedule, maybe this is working? I don’t know….

    Industry observers note that it’s also interesting how the airline actually got permission to operate these routes. As a reminder, Bermuda, Anguilla, and Turks & Caicos, are all British Overseas Territories, and Belize and Jamaica are former British Overseas Territory. How does the airline get permission to serve places like Honduras, though? I guess the airline is somehow getting permission to operate this as fifth freedom service, or something.

    Recent findings suggest that bermudAir is expanding rapidly, as the airline has declared latest routes for the summer of 2027. Not only does this include several new routes to Bermuda (including out of Fredericton!), but the airline is also adding flying between the United States and Grand Cayman, Honduras, Jamaica, etc.

    I think BermudAir deserves an award for the most unusual route network of any “real” airline. I certainly can’t think of any other airline in this “league.”.

All six passengers tragically died in the crash, including four adults and two boys, aged eight and 10.

    Sources indicate that the Cessna involved in the crash took off from Upcoming Orleans at 2:00 PM local time and was bound for Fort Myers, Florida, with the tail number N29002. WVUE, a New Orleans news station, has reported that those onboard were traveling back home after enjoying a fishing trip in Venice, Louisiana.

    Coast Guard responders began a search of the waters over which the aircraft had been flying. They found only three life jackets, an unoccupied life raft, and the plane's floating cabin. Divers then went into the Gulf of Mexico and recovered the bodies of all of those onboard.

    Commander Trevor Blount is the coordinator for the Coast Guard's search and rescue operations in the Mobile area. He mentioned that the situation is heartbreaking. "We are grateful for the strong inter-agency coordination that enabled us to swiftly locate those aboard the aircraft and provide closure to their families," he said.

    The FAA and NTSB have started their investigation into the accident. Some information has already started to emerge. For example, the Coast Guard has remarked the aircraft was falling at a rate of 10,000 feet (3,050 m) per minute when it crashed.

    The FAA's database indicates that the aircraft is registered to EAB Services, who are based in Cape Coral, Florida. It was active for the past week, safely completing a few trips. This included Fort Myers to Buras, Louisiana on November 21, and Fort Myers to East Rutherfordton, North Carolina (outbound and return) on November 19.

    A preliminary report will be available shortly on the authority's Preliminary Accident and Incident Notices webpage. The table below shows the number of Cessnas involved in accidents and incidents over eight days that had them according to this page:.

The 737 MAX was climbing out of Palm Springs International Airport (PSP) and bound for Vancouver International Airport (YVR).

    The pilots received a resolution advisory at approximately 11,400 feet (3,500 m) to climb an additional 600 feet (183 m), allowing the two planes to reach a safe amount of separation. Luckily, the two aircraft were kept apart from each other. However, the Cessna's identity and the minimum distance that separated the two aircraft remains unclear.     It has been revealed that president Trump makes no secret of his desire to punish broadcasters whose content he dislikes. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Chair Brendan Carr is a willing partner, going so far as to threaten the licenses of Disney-owned ABC stations with an early renewal proceeding. This highly unusual move (purportedly for unlawful discrimination) followed President Trump’s demand that ABC and NBC affiliates lose their broadcast licenses for unfavorable coverage of him.

    In a recent development, how did we get to a point where the president and FCC chair can threaten a broadcaster’s license over disfavored content? Two features of federal law enable this abuse: a vague public interest standard open to broad, subjective interpretation, and an archaic equal time rule.

    Brian A. Rankin is an adjunct fellow with the Competitive Enterprise Institute.

    On “The Public Interest Demands Free Speech for Broadcasters”.

    Recent findings suggest that russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump arrive for a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday. (Win McNamee/AFP via Getty Images).

    That was the greeting, complete with a lengthy handshake, President Donald Trump gave Vladimir Putin before two high-level meetings Thursday, including the first “trilateral” session with sitting U.S., Russian and Chinese heads of state.

    “It’s nice to see you,” Trump told Putin before a private one-on-one meeting in China’s Shenzhen economic zone, before pulling the Russian strongman close and saying something into his ear too low for journalists’ microphones to pick up.

    Trump and Putin then posed for the cameras with wide grins, again underscoring the U.S. president’s closeness with a world leader who has been partially shunned by the West since he introduced a war with Ukraine in February 2022. Trump on Thursday also appeared several times alongside Chinese President Xi Jinping, who like Putin has been scorned by Republican and Democratic lawmakers for years.

    Sources indicate that “We’ve had a great relationship for many years. We've known each other for a long time. And I think a lot of wonderful things can come out of this — or, at least, start,” Trump told reporters as Putin beamed from a few feet away.

    They later were joined by Xi for a group photo before sitting down at a round wooden table with a large arrangement of pink flowers in the center.

    Industry observers note that his interactions with and comments about Putin and Xi reflect Trump’s belief that his personal relationships can bend them toward U.S. interests. But that gambit clashed Thursday with his second term’s expiration date — the White House did not disclose any agreements reached during his various meetings with the two leaders, nor did Trump hold a press conference following the three-way session.

    It has been revealed that both Putin and Xi are adept at playing the geopolitical long game. The 26 months left in Trump’s term is a relatively short amount of time compared to the duo that has been in power for a combined 56 years and will remain in place for the foreseeable future.

    Indeed, even Trump acknowledged the first-ever meeting might not immediately yield much progress on its ostensible goal: paring each powers’ nuclear weapons arsenals.

    “I must say, it's, quite frankly, a very hard thing to do, because once you have the nuclear weapons, it's very hard to not have them. It's very hard to give them up as the leader of a country,” Trump noted as Putin and Xi looked on. “Something that's very difficult to say, because … it's the way life works.

    “You know, you have thousands of weapons and you're supposed to give them up, and yet you have countries in addition to us, in much smaller numbers, but they have nuclear weapons, also,” he added. “So it's not an easy thing to do and give them up.”.

    Trump, who was convicted by a Latest York jury in a business records case and who saw a federal election interference case against him dismissed only because of his reelection, also appeared to join Putin’s resistance to international criminal justice entities that have alleged Putin has committed war crimes in Ukraine.

    Industry observers note that “In another area of potential cooperation between us, I'll be suggesting ways to protect our nations’ sovereignty from rogue globalist organizations such as the International Criminal Court, which has gotten out of control, which I believe we all agree has really strayed far from beyond its jurisdiction,” Trump said, a statement that would be almost unthinkable to hear from any other sitting U.S. president.

    Sources indicate that other world leaders, including democratically elected ones, at two Pacific region economic summits in which Trump participated this week did not receive the kind of cordial and personal treatment from the U.S. side that Putin and Xi enjoyed.

    And other world leaders and congressional Democrats this week expressed concern with Trump's closeness to the Russian and Chinese strongmen.

    Sources indicate that senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., on Thursday called the unprecedented summit a “historic embarrassment.” He criticized Trump for leaving the meeting without any apparent concrete commitments from Moscow or Beijing on a number of concerns, including curbing Chinese espionage inside U.S. companies and ending the Ukraine conflict.

    “This summit was nothing but a glorified photo op and a gift to Putin and Xi,” Schumer said.

    Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk wrote this Thursday on X, shortly after Trump’s warm greeting for the former KGB officer: “God, protect us from such friends.”.

    According to recent reports, nicolas Burns, a former senior U.S. diplomatic official under GOP and Democratic presidents, was critical of Trump’s meetings with Xi. He said it was “important” for U.S. and Chinese leaders to hold talks, but added: “We need stability in the relationship with China — but there’s a but.”.

    In a recent development, “The president seems to be following a detente policy with China, with very little substance. There’s a lot of pomp and circumstance, red carpets, a lot of nice words,” the former ambassador to China, NATO and Greece told “Morning Joe” on MS NOW. “Too friendly with Xi Jinping, who’s not going to be swayed by rosy words from President Trump.”.

    Even before Trump met with the Russian and Chinese leaders behind closed doors, Republican and Democratic lawmakers mentioned they doubted very much would come from it.

    “I want nuclear weapons to be reduced. As you know, China has been unwilling to even have a conversation with the United States about nuclear arms reduction until they reach a certain plateau in the number of weapons that they have,” House Armed Services Committee Vice Chair Rob Wittman, R-Va., told reporters Tuesday.

    According to recent reports, “I'm glad that they're willing to have the conversation. We do need a limit, as you know,” added Wittman, who lost his reelection bid earlier this month. “Right now, neither Russia nor China has a nuclear arms reduction treaty with the United States. It would be nice for us to actually have one.”.

    Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., an Armed Services Committee member, wanted Trump to press Putin over Ukraine.

    Industry observers note that “Ukraine is defending itself from Putin's aggression, which this president should be opposing as well,” Blumenthal said Tuesday. “We are spending no money on Ukraine. Let's be very clear: Arms to Ukraine are purchased by Ukraine with financial support from Europe, not America. … Let's support Ukraine.”.

    Sources indicate that on spending, Trump and administration officials have been pressing Senate Republicans to promptly pass another budget reconciliation measure with $350 billion more for the Defense Department. However, Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., and other GOP senators have signaled in the last 24 hours that they had shelved the notion of another fast-track spending measure.

    “You have to have a path forward. You've got to get on it, and you have to protect it, and that takes 50 in the Senate,” Thune told reporters Thursday. “And then you've got to get it through the House. As you probably saw yesterday, a lot of folks in the House were lobbing grenades at the Senate reconciliation bill and complaints about it not being offset, et cetera. So, you know, in my view at least, you want to have a path forward to success.”.

    Over the weekend, I booked an expensive ticket for my dad, brother, and me, from Buenos Aires (EZE) to Santiago (SCL), only to come across a better deal after I’d booked. I called customer service to cancel within the 24-hour cooling-off period, but was refused a refund for the most convoluted and unnecessary reason.

    LATAM is the airline I’ve flown with the second most in my life after British Airways, my old home airline. It’s an airline I look forward to flying with for several reasons. However, this recent booking experience has uncovered a gaping hole in its customer service, which in the air I’ve always found to be excellent.

    This whole situation could have been avoided if I’d been able to pay with my UK credit card on LATAM’s Brazilian website.

    The Brazilian site has no concern when entering UK credit card details.

    However, the default setting for postcodes (ZIP codes) is numerical-only because, as in the US, Brazil’s postcodes consist only of numbers. In the UK, they’re made up of letters and numbers, so I couldn’t add the postcode that my credit card is registered to.

    Sources indicate that I tried using only the numbers of my postcode (the one in the example above is random), but the site returned an error, saying it failed to connect to my bank. My guess would be this wouldn’t be a problem for US credit cards, given that ZIP codes consist only of numbers too.

    I remember this happening previously, but I never had an issue with a booking that I couldn’t change online.

    Ideally, I would have paid with a Brazilian bank account or credit card, but I’m still working through the immigration bureaucracy required to open one.

    First of all, I tried to cancel by logging into my LATAM Pass account, but was redirected to the contact center. This is when I realized how much of an obstacle my booking via the UK website would be.

    After being put on hold 3 times for what seemed like forever, the agent I spoke with at LATAM’s Brazilian call center told me there was nothing she could do to help me.

    She explained the only way I’d get a refund was to call the UK call center, since I’d paid in GBP on the UK website. I called just before the cut-off of the 24-hour cooling-off period, so by then I had exceeded it. I had only left it so close to the cooling-off period because I was researching the trip again the following day and found a better deal; otherwise, I wouldn’t have wanted to cancel.

    According to recent reports, if I had called sooner and had more time, I could have asked someone in the UK to call for me, as my Brazilian phone number can’t make outgoing international calls. I did top up my UK SIM Card with 20 GBP, but at a charge of 2 GBP per minute, the call disconnected after 10 minutes on hold with no answer.

    It has been revealed that irrespective of whether I could have found an easier way to contact the UK call center, I can’t help but feel that my concern should have been resolved there and then over the phone by the Brazilian call center agent. After all, I booked directly through the airline’s website, and then called the airline directly to cancel. It makes no logical sense!

    Because of a stupidly convoluted system, I’m stuck with a LATAM ticket that I can no longer cancel, even though I called customer service within the 24-hour cooling-off period.

    It’s not the end of the world, as we can still take the flights we’d originally booked, but it’s so frustrating to be put in a situation like this in 2026 because of such an archaic technicality.

    I’m still a significant fan of LATAM itself, and will continue to fly it, at least until my Platinum status runs out next year.

    What’s the most frustrating post-sale customer service experience you’ve had?

    @Ben I’m unsure if already mentioned but as a Canadian who has this issue on some sites (ie united app but not their website) and at American movie theatres and gas stations…. Try taking the numbers of your postal code, as you did, and then adding 0’s at the end to get to the required number of characters. That works every time for Canadians in the USA.

    I also don't get a refund after 24 hours passed.

    According to recent reports, I have so many questions. You mention that you couldn't enter your credit card details due to the format of your ZIP code, yet, somehow the ticket was issued?
