    Orient Express Sailing Yachts Review: Corinthian’s Suites, Dining, Amenities, Service, And More

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 35 min read (6916 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~35 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • For the main event of my Orient Express adventure via Africa trip, Ford and I had the chance to spend four nights on the Corinthian, which is the first ship in Orient Express’ fresh cruising venture, known as Orient Express Sailing Yachts.
    • Orient Express Sailing Yachts set sail in the summer of 2026, and with just 54 suites that can accommodate up to 110 guests, it really brings luxury cruising to a upcoming level.
    • I also recently reviewed Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection, and had a great experience, and reviewed Four Seasons Yachts, which is definitely more luxurious, but also has some growing pains.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    For the main event of my Orient Express adventure via Africa trip, Ford and I had the chance to spend four nights on the Corinthian, which is the first ship in Orient Express’ fresh cruising venture, known as Orient Express Sailing Yachts.

    Orient Express Sailing Yachts set sail in the summer of 2026, and with just 54 suites that can accommodate up to 110 guests, it really brings luxury cruising to a upcoming level. It’s a fascinating time for the luxury cruising industry more broadly, given how competition has been heating up.

    I also recently reviewed Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection, and had a great experience, and reviewed Four Seasons Yachts, which is definitely more luxurious, but also has some growing pains. Lastly, I’ve compared all the experiences as well.

    In a recent development, while Orient Express Sailing Yachts is the highest priced cruising venture to date, I have to say, the experience really is unbelievably good, and at least you feel like you’re getting an amazing experience. I come into these kinds of trips with a critical eye, and I was just blown away by the ship’s design, the quality of the food and drinks, and the service. To me the ship felt like a step back in time (in terms of its classic elegance), while also being cutting edge modern.

    If you can swing this experience, I’d highly recommend it. Okay, enough of an intro, here comes my 8,500-word review (yikes, this is the longest review I’ve ever published of anything).

    Recent findings suggest that orient Express Sailing Yachts charges per suite (rather than per person, based on double occupancy), and you’ll find that journeys typically cost an average of $4,000-6,000 per cabin per night for a base suite. Make no mistake, this is the very top end of the cruise market, and at this point you’re paying safari prices for the experience.

    Let me also emphasize that rates go up from there, and Orient Express Sailing Yachts has some of the most insane suites you’ll find at sea, some of which can cost six figures per sailing. Right now, Orient Express offers cruises in Europe in summer, and in the Caribbean in winter, with transatlantic sailings in the spring and fall.

    Recent findings suggest that for what it’s worth, you’ll find rate parity regardless of which booking channel you reserve through. So your best bet is to book through a travel advisor affiliated with Accor Preferred, because they can add perks to your journey. The size of the credit depends on the accommodation type booked, plus the length of the journey.

    Industry observers note that in the interest of full disclosure, Ford was invited on this Orient Express Sailing Yachts journey (due to the amount of volume he books), and I tagged along with him. All opinions expressed are my own, and I initiative to review this exactly the same way I reviewed the two previous cruises (which we paid full price for). I haven’t been asked to write anything, and I have no incentive to be anything other than honest. If people are going to drop a ton of money on a luxury cruise, I want to make sure they’re at least getting the best experience possible.

    We experienced Orient Express Sailing Yachts in early October 2026, shortly before the ship’s transatlantic sailing. Admittedly it wasn’t the most exciting itinerary, but that’s just what worked out for us in terms of timing, since we wanted to minimize our time away from home, had to schedule it around when family could best be with our kids, etc. Below is the itinerary for the sailing we took.

    In a recent development, we were happy with this itinerary, since our primary goal was to see the ship. It definitely wasn’t the most exciting, though, given that we docked at the port in Mahón (rather than tendering), and it also meant we didn’t have a marina day (not that you’d necessarily want that in October, since it’s a bit chillier). But the point is that if you’re traveling more in peak season, you can expect a marina day more consistently.

    Historically, cruising has been all about offering an all-inclusive experience. That’s true with Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection, but then Four Seasons Yachts countered the trend, by only including breakfast, and then charging extra for lunch, dinner, and drinks (I don’t love this concept, especially given the quality complications they have).

    While Orient Express Sailing Yachts might charge a lot, what I really appreciate is how the company has an ultra all-inclusive concept, to an extent that’s even greater than you’ll find on most other cruise lines. Orient Express Sailing Yachts journeys include the following:.

    Orient Express Sailing Yachts journeys don’t include the following:.

    Regarding the Orient Express Sailing Yachts tipping policy, the company states that gratuities are included in the fare — “however, if you wish to offer a tip as an extra gesture of appreciation, it will be warmly received.”.

    Recent findings suggest that I just have to emphasize that the level of inclusions really impressed me. Seriously, I was served caviar with breakfast, lunch, and dinner at various points (and even cocktails!), and the house champagne is Veuve Clicquot La Grande Dame 2018 (which retails for around $200 per bottle).

    Orient Express Sailing Yachts at the moment has a single ship, which is named the Corinthian (a second ship is being introduced in 2027, and it’ll be named the Olympian).

    It has been revealed that the ship entered service in 2026, and is 722 feet (220 meters) long, 82 feet (25 meters) wide, and 26,600 gross tons. With 54 accommodations and a maximum capacity of around 110 guests, there’s a roughly 1.5:1 staff to guest ratio, given that there are around 170 staff onboard. The spaciousness of this ship, and the amount of space allocated to each passenger, really is next level.

    In a recent development, the Corinthian also has the title of being the world’s largest sailing yacht, as it has three automated SolidSail rigid sails on tilting carbon masts, to provide wind propulsion, alongside hybrid LNG auxiliary power. It’s just such an elegant and distinctive looking ship, that it can’t help but turn heads. For those curious, it was explained that the sails reduce emissions by around 10%, and no, the ship doesn’t “heel” in the way a smaller sailboat would. Unless you’re looking up, you wouldn’t realize there are even sails.

    You can find the full Corinthian deck proposal here. As you’d expect for a sail boat, there aren’t quite as many floors as on a traditional cruise ship. Guests can access a total of five floors, between levels three and seven. To briefly cover that:.

    According to recent reports, near the ship’s entrance, you’ll find a very cool directory of sorts, which shows the floorplan of the ship. You can click any amenity, and then it will light up, so that’s super handy.

    Sources indicate that the ship has two sets of elevator banks, as well as two sets of staircases, so getting around the ship is really easy. We always used the stairs, since we were typically within a couple of floors of where we needed to be.

    As you’d expect, the ease of boarding a ship varies greatly depending on its size, but Orient Express Sailing Yachts really took it to the next level in terms of how seamless it was. We had spent a night at the Hôtel Dieu Intercontinental Marseille. Our journey included the transfers, so an Orient Express representative met us at the hotel, and then we were driven to the port.

    It has been revealed that getting onboard the ship literally couldn’t have been easier. There were no formalities in the port, but instead, we were escorted straight through security, and then check-in was handled once onboard.

    There were no other guests as we boarded, and the staff really went above and beyond — for example, the crew member who escorted us through security and onto the ship insisted on holding an umbrella over our heads, to shade us from the sun.

    Our check-in process onboard took all of five minutes, and at that point we were introduced to our butler, Reuben, who escorted us to our suite, and took care of everything from there. I should mention how Reuben was German, so they specifically appointed us a German butler, which I thought was super fun (so we communicated with him exclusively in German).

    Sources indicate that we didn’t have a stop that involved tendering, but for those situations where you do, it’s an efficient process, given how few guests there are. Our one stop had us docked in port, and there was a nice seating area outside the ship with bottled water, sunscreen, etc. Admittedly a setup like this is more useful when you’re waiting on a tender, rather than just walking directly onto or off the ship.

    Orient Express Sailing Yachts has 54 suites onboard, spread across over a dozen different categories. The entry level suites here are among the most spacious at sea, while the penthouse suites really take luxury and space to the next level.

    It has been revealed that our sailing was rather empty — only 19 of the 54 suites were occupied — and we were upgraded to a higher suite category (I believe they had blocked most of the entry level room categories, as they were doing some minor updates to them ahead of the ship heading to the Caribbean). So let me share my thoughts on that suite first, and then I’ll share some pictures of other suites that I had the opportunity to tour as well.

    In a recent development, we stayed in an Appartement Prestige, which is one of the more premium standard suite categories, but below the duplex suites and penthouse suites. These suites are marketed as being an average of 1,119 square feet (104 square meters), so they’re incredibly spacious.

    We were assigned suite 518, located on the fifth floor. The hallways on the Corinthian are just stunning, as you can see below. It really feels more like a luxury hotel than a ship, especially in terms of the width of the hallway.

    The concept of forgetting that one is on a ship continued inside the suite. The interior felt more to me like a “Palace” hotel in France, than what you’d expect at sea. I can’t even imagine how much money was spent on the interiors, as the quality of the finishes, from the wall treatments to the carpet, as well as the furniture, was just unreal.

    In a recent development, upon entering the suite, there was first a dining area with a table and a chair, as well as a desk with a chair (that chair could also be moved over to the dining table). It’s not often you get this kind of space in a cruise ship suite.

    Sources indicate that the minibar was also in this area, and was well stocked, with everything being complimentary. This included a Nespresso coffee machine, cocktails, wine, beer, soft drinks, etc. They were also happy to replenish the minibar however you wanted, so there are really no limits.

    Industry observers note that that entry area then flowed into the living room, which was gorgeous. It had a couch and a coffee table, as well as a hidden TV (which would pop up from in front of the mirror).

    Waiting on the dining table was a lovely welcome amenity, consisting of some freshly baked treats, a fruit plate, and a bottle of Veuve Clicquot 2015 Rose. There was also an Orient Express branded journal, along with two Orient Express water bottles, which guests could take home.

    Double doors then led into the bedroom, which had a very plush king size bed.

    Much like with the bedroom, the bathroom will make you forget that you’re on a ship, as it had double sinks, a soaking tub, a walk-in shower with amazing water pressure, and a toilet in a separate room.

    There were also a couple of closet areas, so there was plenty of space to store luggage and clothes.

    The suite then had a balcony that stretched the entire length of the suite, with very comfortable furniture.

    Industry observers note that beyond the generally beautiful design, it has to be pointed out just how over the top everything was. I mean, the deck furniture uses fabrics from Loro Piana, just to give you a sense of just how high-end it is.

    Housekeeping in the room was great (it was taken care of twice daily, and always well timed), butler service was very useful (more on that a bit later, when I talk about service), Starlink Wi-Fi was lightning fast, and I also love how Orient Express Sailing Yachts includes laundry. You could get unlimited washing, dry cleaning, etc., so that’s a very nice feature.

    According to recent reports, in the interest of checking out different suite products, I also had the chance to tour the Suite Panoramique, which is the entry level accommodation onboard, located on levels four and five. These are 506 square feet (47 square meters), so they’re spacious for an entry level suite on a cruise.

    Industry observers note that this had the same general design concept as the suite we were in, except there wasn’t a fully separate living area. The suite had a comfortable king size bed, a desk with a chair, a dining table, and a huge window with a double daybed of sorts.

    While there was no bathtub, the bathroom still had double sinks, a walk-in shower, and a toilet in a separate room.

    According to recent reports, to point out the obvious, these entry level suites don’t have balconies. Of course people prefer to have balconies, but this is just a simple reality of the difference between sailboats and cruise ships, in terms of how many levels there are, how far above water they are, etc.

    Orient Express Sailing Yachts’ top end suites are really next level, so I also had the chance to tour the Zephyr Suite, which is located on level seven, and is the second most premium suite onboard. This two bedroom suite has 2,486 square feet (231 square meters) of interior space, plus a terrace that’s 1,206 square feet (112 square meters).

    According to recent reports, what I thought was so cool was how unique the design of this suite was, as the top suite products seem to have a totally original design. This very much had a residential vibe, with a long hallway connecting the various parts of the suite.

    Seriously, check out this living room….

    However, perhaps the coolest feature was the replica of an Orient Express Heritage cabin, intended to pay homage to the legendary train.

    Recent findings suggest that the Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian has two pools onboard, with one being rather traditional, and one being unlike anything else at sea (at least to my knowledge). The main “leisure” pool is located on the fifth floor, at the back of the ship. While the pool has beautiful aesthetics and lovely deck space around it, this isn’t some destination pool in and of itself. So if a huge pool is a crucial factor in picking a ship, Four Seasons Yachts might be a better option.

    Industry observers note that we’re all different, and personally, I’m not much of a pool person. Quite to the contrary, I actually loved this pool deck, since it was mostly covered and in the shade, so I could nicely sit there and enjoy the breeze (funny enough, Four Seasons Yachts has an amazing pool, but I didn’t actually spend much time there, due to the lack of shade).

    It has been revealed that the ship then has a second pool, which is among the most memorable you’ll find on any ship. The lap pool is 54 feet (16 meters) long, and it’s located under the sails. It really feels like you’re in a cave, since it’s on a deck that’s one level down from the main upper deck. What a pool!

    On the pool front, really my only disappointment was the lack of a hot tub. As much as I find hot tubs to be kind of gross, I do love them, especially on a ship, so I was sad there wasn’t one of those. In general, the newer ultra high end cruise lines seem to be lacking in that department (the same was true on Four Seasons Yachts).

    It has been revealed that beyond the pool setup, on the seventh floor you’ll find a huge deck you can hang out on. There are lots of lounge chairs out here, though it’s not necessarily that popular for just lounging around. The star of the show here is what’s above.

    According to recent reports, the time when the deck really gets popular is when the ship pulls into or out of ports, given the panoramic views from up here, plus the ability to watch the sails be lowered and raised. I must say, it was absolutely mesmerizing to watch. They made a big event of departures, with live music, cocktails, etc. It really felt like a cocktail reception, only more intimate.

    Recent findings suggest that speaking of deck space, another fun aspect of the ship is how you can actually just freely walk up to the deck in front of the bridge, and even all the way to the bow. How fun!

    According to recent reports, the Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian wellness complex is located on the fourth floor, and that includes a Guerlain Spa. This area is an impressive 5,380 square feet (500 square meters), with four treatment suites (including a double suite), as well as all kinds of other traditional spa facilities.

    Guests can always use the facilities, even without an appointment, and that includes a sauna, steam room, relaxation area, locker rooms, etc.

    The spa treatment rooms are absolutely gorgeous, whether we’re talking about the couples room, or the individual ones.

    Ford and I got a couples massage during our final day (where we were at sea), and I can honestly say it was one of the best spa treatments I’ve ever had. Not only was the therapist I had incredible, but the massage bed was so comfortable, and there was something so calming about the view, the gentle sway of the ship, etc.

    For those curious about the pricing, you can find part of the spa menu below.

    According to recent reports, the ship also has a full hair salon and barber shop, so there are no shortage of opportunities to get your grooming needs taken care of here. The barber shop even leads to the speakeasy — more on that later.

    In a recent development, the Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian has a gym located on the fourth floor, which can be accessed by guests 24/7. The gym isn’t huge, but is more than sufficient given the size of the ship, in my opinion. Every time we used it, we were alone.

    The gym had a good selection of cardio and weight equipment, as well as a separate room for aerobics, boxing, etc.

    There was an excellent personal trainer onboard, and it was possible to schedule sessions with him at no extra cost. So it’s not just for group fitness, but even for personal sessions, on a space available basis. That’s really nice, as virtually any other cruise would charge for that, in my experience.

    The Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian has an incredibly impressive entertainment area, located on deck four. The matter is, it’s not really used a whole lot. Now, I’m not sure I’d actually call this an “issue,” but let me explain.

    When you think of mega cruise ships, nightly shows and entertainment are among the most popular attractions. The thing is, the smaller the ship is, the less interest there is in things like this, and that’s especially true for the cruise lines that are primarily targeted at people who haven’t historically been cruisers.

    So the Corinthian has a huge theater with dozens of seats, but there’s not a whole lot that goes on there.

    Perhaps the more interesting entertainment feature is the private cinema, where you can have them screen a movie (or whatever) for you.

    There’s even a recording studio onboard — what a cool concept, and in addition to being able to play instruments here, I heard people have used this to record podcasts, etc.

    On the topic of entertainment, the ship also has a card room on the fourth floor, with chess, checkers, decks of cards, etc.

    Separately, there’s also the yacht club, which is basically a very elegant lounge area where guests can hang out, watch TV, etc.

    It has been revealed that lastly, the ship has the library on the fourth floor, which has an incredible selection of books. Everything on the Corinthian is so thoughtful, including the book selection. As it was explained to us, the 1,500-book library is supposed to represent the most key books of the century, and were curated by the historic Parisian bookshop Galignani.

    I know there’s sometimes confusion about whether Orient Express Sailing Yachts is kids friendly, and the answer is… sort of.

    According to recent reports, on most voyages, guests onboard must be 16 years of age or older. However, on dedicated family voyages, children ages six months to 15 years old are allowed as well. Infants under six months aren’t permitted onboard, and per the terms, “families traveling with little ones under two years old must be accompanied by a dedicated babysitter throughout their voyage.”.

    Quite honestly, it’s logical that Orient Express Sailing Yachts would have this policy, since the ship’s venues feel really intimate, the pools aren’t huge, etc.

    For family voyages, the Corinthian does have a kids club onboard, which offers activities with a dedicated team. Babysitting services can also be arranged for excursions or gala evenings. But in terms of being kids friendly, I definitely think it’s an area where Four Seasons Yachts wins, as all voyages are kids friendly, the pool is huge, and there’s both a kids club and teens club.

    In a recent development, orient Express Sailing Yachts has an incredibly impressive selection of restaurants, bars, and lounges onboard, with the culinary vision overseen by well-known chef Yannick Alléno. Before I get into details, let me just say that I found the quality of food and drinks onboard to be truly exceptional.

    I try not to exaggerate, because I think far too many people are a little too generous when describing food on cruises (or flights, for that matter — what’s with all these people describing airplane food as Michelin dining?). However, I found the quality of catering on Orient Express Sailing Yachts to just be in a completely different league than Four Seasons Yachts.

    I was also delighted by the generosity of the included options, with an incredible alcohol selection, caviar accompanying dishes at breakfast, lunch, and dinner (and even cocktails), etc. It’s also interesting to note that no reservations are allowed onboard, except at the fine dining restaurant that costs extra.

    Everything was always available whenever we wanted it, though people will otherwise probably have mixed feelings on that policy (conversely, the concern when you do allow reservations is that people hog them and then just cancel at the last minute, leaving other guests with limited options).

    Anyway, here are the most significant outlets onboard Orient Express Sailing Yachts:.

    With that out of the way, let’s get into the venues in a bit more detail.

    La Terrasse is Orient Express Sailing Yachts’ all-day dining restaurant, serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner. It’s located at the back of the sixth floor, and has both indoor and outdoor seating. The fact that this is the casual restaurant really tells you the quality of the experience, as there are white tablecloths all hours of the day.

    This is the primary restaurant where breakfast is served, and you can find that menu below.

    Breakfast is entirely a la carte, though at the start of the meal, a basket with a rotating selection of croissants and pastries was brought out.

    There was a large selection of fresh juices and coffee available. My one disappointment was that the coffee was just okay, and clearly came from a machine. That’s ironic, because there’s plenty of delicious barista coffee on the ship, so this seems to be one of the only venues where that’s the case. Given the quality of service onboard, I’m sure they’d also be happy to get you a coffee from somewhere else, if you prefer.

    We found the breakfast selection to be very good, and over the course of our stay tried the acai bowl with coconut and seasonal fruit, chia pudding with fresh mango, the mixed berry plate, the crispy and soft blinis with caviar cream and smoked salmon, the avocado toast, and more.

    We also came to La Terrasse one day for lunch, and you can find that menu below.

    Recent findings suggest that we split the chickpea hummus with parmesan to start, and then had the smoked salmon club sandwich and Thai beef salad as our mains. At our server’s insistence, we finished off with a floating island for dessert. YUM.

    We also had dinner here our first evening, and you can find that menu below.

    To start, we had the smoked salmon with blinis and sour cream, and the gazpacho.

    Then for mains, we had the pepper crusted beef fillet with cognac and cream sauce, and the red tuna teriyaki style, along with some sides.

    Lastly, we finished off the meal with a selection from the cheese trolley, plus the vanilla millefeuille.

    Across the board, the food and service were exceptional, so it’s amazing that this is just the most basic restaurant onboard, as it only gets better from there.

    L’Ecrin is Orient Express Sailing Yachts’ elevated dinner restaurant, with a focus on seafood and pasta. It’s located on the sixth floor, and it exclusively has indoor seating. This restaurant doesn’t cost extra, but in my opinion is on par with the paid restaurant on some of the other top ships.

    We went here one evening for dinner, and you can find the menu below.

    In a recent development, at the start of the meal, we were offered some sinfully delicious bread, along with some cured meats. I’ll talk more about service in a bit, but I might as well just mention in passing how good the crew was about our dietary preferences. For example, we mentioned when we boarded how we don’t eat pork, so without having to say anything, we were brought something that fit our needs.

    In a recent development, we took an unusual approach to ordering. To start, we shared the seabass carpaccio with citrus marinade, and the spaghetti with caviar. My gosh, not only was the caviar portion on the spaghetti massive, but the overall flavor of the dish was incredible, as the beurre blanc combined with caviar had quite the unique flavor profile.

    Then for mains, we had the warm lobster with olive oil and mayonnaise and the caponata and polenta. Again, this was very, very good.

    For dessert, while I had heard amazing things about the suzette pasta (flambeed tableside), we decided on the signature bronte pistachio ice cream coupe, which was insanely indulgent.

    In a recent development, what a meal! This was definitely my favorite restaurant onboard.

    La Table by Yannick Alléno is Orient Express Sailing Yachts’ most premium dinner restaurant, and it’s the only venue that comes at an extra charge, at the rate of €400 per person for the tasting menu.

    In a recent development, first, we have to talk about the restaurant as such. Can you believe this is on a ship? This is without a doubt the most beautiful dining venue I’ve ever seen on a ship. With just over half a dozen tables, it’s also a really intimate space.

    The tasting menu is constantly changing, and you can find the menu for our dinner below.

    I’ll let the pictures speak for themselves….

    The meal was very good, with service that matched the food quality. It really felt like a Michelin-starred dining experience in terms of the presentation, the service flow, etc.

    In a recent development, while this was excellent, I will say, I wouldn’t necessarily feel compelled to dine here again. That’s just because the standard restaurants are so great that I don’t necessarily think it’s worth the incremental cost. At a minimum, don’t feel like you’re missing out if you don’t eat here… but definitely do take a look at the restaurant, to appreciate its beauty!

    L’Encre is Orient Express Sailing Yachts’ venue that’s exclusively open for lunch, and it was definitely my favorite lunch spot onboard. It’s basically a circular counter with a little over a dozen seats, so the setting is stunning.

    You can find the menu below. Think of the concept as basically being like a seafood omakase, where they just keep bringing you out more dishes. Of course you can customize however you want, ask for more of whatever you really like, skip dishes, etc. Below is a sampling of what we ate.

    La Piscine Lounge is Orient Express Sailing Yachts’ poolside venue, serving drinks, snacks, and even full meals, throughout most of the day. It’s even opening at night, and can double as a bar for a pre-dinner drink. It’s a beautiful space, definitely not your typical pool bar!

    You can find the drink list and menu for that below.

    We had an afternoon snack here one day, and split the mezze and the veggie burger, both of which were very good.

    Le Bar de la Bibliotheque is Orient Express Sailing Yachts’ coffee shop in the library area, and it’s a lovely place from which to get some work done, read a book, etc.

    Here you’ll find barista coffee, homemade cakes, fresh juices, kombucha, and more.

    Industry observers note that le Wagon Bar is Orient Express Sailing Yachts’ primary bar venue, and it’s only open late at night. It’s intended to be a replica of the circular bar found on the modern Orient Express trains, with 1920s and 1930s heritage craftsmanship, so it’s a very cool space.

    It has been revealed that there’s a DJ there at night. The one thing to be aware of is that it only opens really late (9:30PM at the earliest, but often 10PM), and if you’re on a quieter sailing, there might not be too much of a vibe here. However, I’ve heard that on other sailings this place can be packed — it’s all about the crowd on a particular cruise.

    You can find the drink list below.

    I ordered the signature Corinthian Martini, with gin, vodka, champagne cordial, and — naturally, like everything on this ship — caviar!

    Next, Le Speakeasy Bar is Orient Express Sailing Yachts’ speakeasy. The idea is basically that people do a bar crawl, and it’s common to move between both bars in the same evening. Much like Le Wagon Bar, this one also opens really late.

    The bar is located through a hidden door in the barbershop, so they’re really committed to that speakeasy theme.

    This bar even has a separate smoking room, which I’m sure smokers will appreciate (as it’s the only indoor space on the ship where you can smoke).

    This bar also has some unique signature cocktails, and you can find that drink list below.

    While not included, they are very proud of their liquor selection here, with some bottles that are older than my dad (and at a cost of up to $2,400 per shot — yowzers!).

    Tempted as I was, I stuck to one of the included martinis. 😉.

    Le Flybridge Bar is Orient Express Sailing Yachts’ outdoor bar space located on the top floor. While this is open quite frequently, it really only gets busy when the ship sets sail, given the interest in watching the sails in action.

    Recent findings suggest that orient Express Sailing Yachts of course has 24/7 room service, which is included, with no additional costs. The standard room service menu is on the basic side, but service very much falls into the category of them wanting to make guests happy, so they’re also happy to get you something from any restaurant, if you’d like (but since the menus are always changing, they’re not published in the room service menu).

    We did have room service dinner one evening….

    …and the final morning we had breakfast in our suite as well (we accidentally ordered too much).

    Our amazing butler, Reuben, also gladly brought us cappuccinos and protein shakes, so they were happy to accommodate guests however they could.

    Orient Express Sailing Yachts has a very impressive included drink menu. You can find the standard alcoholic drink list below, though some venues have additional options or signature cocktails customized to that venue.

    Having Veuve Clicquot La Grande Dame 2018 as the house champagne is very impressive. And let me just say, they’re also not cheap with the pours — you can barely go anywhere without having a glass pushed on you. 😉.

    Of course there’s also a premium drink list with even more special wines and spirits, and those come at an extra cost.

    I have to acknowledge that our sailing was rather empty, so the staff to guest ratio on this sailing was unreal. That being noted, it wasn’t just the ratio that was amazing, but the quality of staff was really incredible as well. If you don’t have good staff, they’ll find a way to disappoint even if the staff to guest ratio is amazing.

    I’m not exaggerating when I say that service on Orient Express Sailing Yachts was flawless in terms of attention to detail, and that was such a contrast to our Four Seasons Yachts experience.

    It’s hard to even pinpoint any one area that impressed me, because it was just very consistent, polished, and proactive, across the board. Let me just give a few examples:.

    As I said in my Four Seasons Yachts review, while we had an amazing time, we had way more service issues than I’d consider to be acceptable, given the price point. This was exactly the opposite, and it was just flawless service experience after flawless service experience. So while I’m sure service is consistently good, I’m sure the empty sailing also contributed to taking this to the next level.

    We were definitely on an odd sailing, in terms of seasonality, since we were on the second to last voyage before the ship sailed across the Atlantic, to start the winter season in the Caribbean.

    Our sailing was empty, with just 19 of the 54 suites occupied, so there were fewer than 40 guests. It really felt like having a private yacht, as we rarely saw others, and we’d go to restaurants for dinner, at most a handful of other tables would be occupied.

    On our sailing, almost everyone seemed to be a European retiree, so it was maybe in line with what you’d expect from the stereotypical guest profile of Orient Express trains. However, Ford has had some clients on Orient Express Sailing Yachts, and based on the feedback he has gotten, the ship can be an absolute scene, with some pretty over-the-top people.

    The guest profile that Orient Express Sailing Yachts gets is probably a bit different than almost any other cruise line. For one, the ship has already been chartered multiple times in its first season, so you can imagine the kinds of people we’re talking about. And even on sailings that haven’t been chartered, there have been some A-list people onboard.

    So anyway, we had a very pleasant, understated crowd onboard, but I’ve also heard the crowd can make for quite some people watching, especially for sailings in the South of France, etc.

    It has been revealed that as I mentioned at the beginning, my goal here is to be as objective as possible, so what feedback do I have? Honestly, as much as I have a critical eye, I think there are shockingly few areas for improvements. Here are the things that stood out to me:.

    According to recent reports, I also want to acknowledge that Trek Trendy had published a review of the Orient Express Corinthian, and I think that’s worth watching for a different perspective. I think he was being totally fair with some of his critique, but I had a different experience:.

    I travel a ton, and as much as I have so many amazing experiences, I’m almost always excited to go home, given that I miss family, and travel is sort of my “job.” I have to be honest, the Orient Express Corinthian was the first time in recent memory where I thought to myself “man, I wish it weren’t over.”.

    Earlier this year I experienced Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection and Four Seasons Yachts, and they’re both great in their own ways. However, Orient Express Sailing Yachts is really in a different league. Yes, it’s priced at the top end of the market, but it also includes the most, and I really appreciate that. There’s something nice about paying a high voyage cost in advance, but then feeling like everything is included.

    It has been revealed that orient Express Sailing Yachts really is an unbelievable product, from the design of the ship, to the incredible restaurant and bar concepts, to the service. If you can swing it — and especially if you’ve never taken a cruise before — I can’t recommend this enough.

    What’s your take on the Orient Express cruise concept?

  • The TSA PreCheck Touchless ID program now enables eligible travelers to pass through security checkpoints at over 60 major U.S. airports without presenting a physical ID or boarding pass.
  • This system uses facial comparison technology to match travelers' faces with their passport photos on file, streamlining the security process.
  • To use Touchless ID, travelers must opt in through their airline frequent flyer profile by uploading a passport photo and consenting to facial identification.
  • Availability varies by airline and terminal, so travelers should confirm participation at their departure airport before relying on this service.

  • Not all airlines or terminals at a given airport may offer Touchless ID, so check availability in advance.
  • Travelers should still bring a physical ID, as technical issues or officer requests may require traditional identification.

    #123568. Hakeem Jeffries’s Reckless Medicare Expansion

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (548 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nationalreview ↗ Open Full Page

    Hakeem Jeffries’s Reckless Medicare Expansion

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (548 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nationalreview

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • We have long warned that if Republicans did not get serious about advancing their own vision for health care, Democrats would use their next opportunity to further expand the role of government.
    • It has been revealed that fresh off a sweeping victory in the midterm elections, incoming House Speaker Hakeem Jeffries made a radical proposal.
    • No doubt, with a stampede of newly introduced socialists joining his caucus, Jeffries is trying to get ahead of the left-wing push for a fully government-run system branded as “Medicare for All.” When last nationally debated in 2019, it was estimated to add $34 trillion to existing federal spending with no plausible financing mechanism.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We have long warned that if Republicans did not get serious about advancing their own vision for health care, Democrats would use their next opportunity to further expand the role of government. And here we are.

    It has been revealed that fresh off a sweeping victory in the midterm elections, incoming House Speaker Hakeem Jeffries made a radical proposal. He endorsed lowering the retirement age of Medicare and adding vision, hearing, and dental coverage to the program. Additionally, he noted that the government should provide coverage for all children.

    No doubt, with a stampede of newly introduced socialists joining his caucus, Jeffries is trying to get ahead of the left-wing push for a fully government-run system branded as “Medicare for All.” When last nationally debated in 2019, it was estimated to add $34 trillion to existing federal spending with no plausible financing mechanism.

    At this point, Jeffries’s proposal is theoretical. There’s a significant budgetary difference between lowering the Medicare eligibility age from its current 65 to 60, and lowering it to 50 — as Senator Kirsten Gillibrand and other senators are proposing. There are also questions about what sort of premiums, if any, would be required for near-retirees to “buy in” to the program or how generous the theoretical vision, hearing, and dental benefits would be. Filling in those blanks is the difference between a proposal that costs a few hundred billion dollars and one that costs trillions of dollars.

    But it’s preposterous at this stage to start any discussion of Medicare with a suggestion that spending on the program needs to be increased rather than reined in — especially to cover a population without a high uninsured rate. Over the next decade, the federal government is projected to spend $18.5 trillion on Medicare, making it the largest expenditure apart from that other federal entitlement, Social Security. Medicare no longer collects enough money in payroll taxes to cover current benefits, let alone added benefits that cover more people. Even a more modest lowering of the retirement age to 60 would add over 7 million beneficiaries. On its current trajectory, Medicare’s trust fund (the money it is “owed” by the rest of the government from the days when it was running surpluses) would be exhausted by 2033.

    Medicare is a major driver of the nation’s broader fiscal problem. Already, debt held by the public has eclipsed 100 percent of gross domestic product. By the end of the decade, it is projected to reach 120 percent. By comparison, debt peaked at 106 percent during World War II. Now we are on track to exceed that number, not during a global crisis, but during an ordinary period of relative peace and prosperity. And that’s before Jeffries grabs the gavel with a massive majority behind him.

    Sources indicate that perhaps more concerning, President Trump indicated last week that he may be game for some compromise proposal. “There is a real possibility that we get a lot of great things done, especially on health care,” he said.

    If Trump is serious and actually considers cutting a deal with Democrats to expand Medicare, congressional Republicans should fight it at all costs.

    The Editors comprise the senior editorial staff of National Review magazine and nationalreview.com.

    On “Hakeem Jeffries’s Reckless Medicare Expansion”.

    The House has a latest lame-duck challenge: Attendance

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (695 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that house Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., pictured at the U.S.
    • Republicans who want to accomplish as much as possible before Democrats take control of the House are confronting a fresh challenge: Attendance.
    • Thirty-two members – 21 Republicans, 10 Democrats, and one independent – did not vote in Thursday morning’s session before members headed out of town a day early for Thanksgiving break.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that house Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., pictured at the U.S. Capitol on Thursday, noted attendance is 'a great frustration.' (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    Republicans who want to accomplish as much as possible before Democrats take control of the House are confronting a fresh challenge: Attendance.

    Thirty-two members – 21 Republicans, 10 Democrats, and one independent – did not vote in Thursday morning’s session before members headed out of town a day early for Thanksgiving break. This, a day after House GOP leadership pulled a procedural rule vote when it was clear the vote might fall short because of GOP no-highlights – and then canceled a planned Friday voting session.

    The House has just 12 scheduled voting days left in the 119th Congress. And leaders who have at times struggled to ensure sufficient support for their agenda from the narrow majority now say they will work to make sure cases of senioritis don’t compound the problem, as both returning and nonreturning members have been part of the problem.

    "Attendance is a great frustration for me right now,” House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., told reporters Thursday. “We'll be addressing that with members.".

    “We want to run through the tape and finish strong, but we can't do that unless people are present at work, so that's our challenge,” Johnson continued.

    Sources indicate that of 13 roll call votes in the House since the midterms, all but one has had a double-digit number of no-shows; for five of the 13, more than 30 members did not vote. The average number of members not voting has more than doubled since the midterm elections, compared to the final 13 roll call votes beforehand.

    Sources indicate that johnson has just a few more weeks before he steps out of the spotlight and Judiciary Chairman Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, takes over the GOP conference as minority leader. But his members are still counting on him to get them back to Washington.

    Recent findings suggest that “I think there's going to be some serious conversations over the phone, behind the scenes over the weekend,” Rep. Michael Cloud, R-Texas, noted. “We all took an oath of office. We have a sworn duty to be here. We're still being paid to be here, and you have to show up and do the job.”.

    And it's not just leadership that's frustrated with their missing colleagues this week.

    Industry observers note that “There is, no question,” Rep. Pat Harrigan, R-N.C., who narrowly won reelection, responded when asked whether there was frustration in the caucus over members' absences.

    Industry observers note that “I don't know what you do with people that don't understand the concept of duty,” Harrigan said. “I mean, look, you signed up for a two-year term. You execute your two-year term, no matter what happens along the way politically. You have an obligation both to your constituency and to your country to be here, so the fact that they're not self-motivated to be here, I don't think that there's really much that you can do.”.

    Attendance has also been a bipartisan problem. A group of House Democrats, including members of leadership, faced harsh criticism from party activists for not returning to the chamber in time for a vote related to a resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

    While Republican leadership grapples with the fallout from the party’s election losses earlier this month, lawmakers still face a slew of legislative items as Congress looks ahead to the holidays and a government shutdown looms.

    Many Republicans want to see a party-line defense spending bill cross the finish line, while the NDAA remains in treacherous territory and Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act has been dark for months.

    However, the frustration does not lie solely with absent House members.

    “The Senate needs to do their job,” Rep. John McGuire, R-Va., mentioned. “I know we had a hard time in the midterms. History doesn't favor the party in the president's office, but we passed the Save America Act five times here. It goes over there, nothing. We've got a farm bill, nothing. We got an NDAA. We got so many things.”.

    • Norse Atlantic has today provided an update on its financial situation and ongoing strategic review.
    • It has been revealed that the Tech giant’s financial situation is critical.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, back in August 2026, all-Boeing 787 airline Norse Atlantic Airways announced it was in a rough financial spot, and was pursuing a sale, merger, or other arrangement. Not a whole lot of solutions have been found since then, and it seems like things have only gotten worse. The airline has just revealed the latest regarding its financial situation, and it’s not looking good.

    Norse Atlantic has today provided an update on its financial situation and ongoing strategic review. There’s no point in paraphrasing this, so here’s the direct statement from the airline:.

    It has been revealed that the Tech giant’s financial situation is critical. It is dependent on securing financing to meet its short-term liquidity needs and to continue its operations. Norse, supported by its advisors, has explored various strategic alternatives and entertains discussions for a potential takeover. In parallel, the Board and management have diligently considered other available options, including ACMI contracts. Norse is also engaged in discussions with selected parties on short term financing, however, there can be no assurances that such discussions will result in a viable solution.

    According to recent reports, to state the obvious, this sounds really, really bad. When the firm is publicly stating that its “financial situation is critical” and that it needs to secure financing to meet “short-term liquidity needs,” you know things aren’t good. So we’ll see what comes of this, but it seems like there’s a very real chance the airline could simply liquidate in the coming weeks.

    The airline industry can be a funny business, and there’s no clearer example of that than Norse Atlantic Airways. The airline released in 2022, with the goal of operating long haul, low cost flights, particularly across the Atlantic.

    That wasn’t exactly a unique business model, because this was exactly what Norwegian did, before it discontinued long haul flights in 2021. Not only was the idea sort of copied, but Norse Atlantic had some executives from Norwegian, and even picked up the planes that Norwegian previously flew.

    Industry observers note that but as is all too common in the airline industry, clearly they thought it would be different this time around… it wasn’t. So in 2024 we saw the airline revision its business model, making the focus less about operating regularly scheduled commercial flights, and more about leasing out aircraft, all while reducing its fleet.

    Recent findings suggest that the organization got a lifeline when IndiGo decided to lease some Norse Atlantic 787s to dabble in long haul flying, ahead of the airline taking delivery of its own Airbus A350s. However, between all the airspace closures, high oil costs, and generally declining performance at IndiGo as the airline increasingly moved away from its core strengths, the airline recently decided to scrap that experiment, and stop leasing planes from Norse Atlantic.

    Recent findings suggest that since then, opportunities for Norse Atlantic have been limited. The airline did manage to lease a couple of Dreamliners to the “upcoming” Pakistan International Airlines, but for an airline with 12 planes, that hardly pays the bills.

    In a recent development, norse Atlantic does still operate some of its own flights, but in a very limited capacity. The airline has some flights from Europe to Thailand and the United States, but most are seasonal, and they’re a fraction of what they previously were.

    According to recent reports, really there’s just one idea that comes to mind for me — we know that Southwest Airlines wants to start long haul flights. The airline had been considering a Boeing 787 order, and was possibly even looking at ways to get planes faster than from a direct order (which requires waiting for years).

    Could these dozen Norse Atlantic 787s somehow end up at Southwest? The interiors would just need some updates (assuming the airline wants to offer business class), but talk about a quick way to grow a decent sized fleet.

    Norse Atlantic has released a statement admitting that its “financial situation is critical,” and that the tech giant’s future is “dependent on securing financing to meet short-term liquidity needs.”.

    In a recent development, financial challenges at the tech giant started when… well, it debuted. Norse Atlantic was just a direct replica of Norwegian, which had failed. When the airline realized that the long haul, low cost business model doesn’t really work, they tried to pivot to wet leasing. And while there’s some demand for that, it’s also not a 100% consistent business in terms of demand.

    The tone of this announcement sure is serious, so I’m curious to see how this evolves. I feel bad for the frontline employees at the airline, of course, as they’re the victims in this.

    • Marriott Bonvoy has just revealed its status soft landing policy for the 2027 status year, for situations where someone doesn’t qualify for a particular elite tier based on their activity in 2026.
    • In other words, Ambassador Elites will at most drop to Titanium Elite, Titanium Elites will at most drop to Platinum Elite, Platinum Elites will at most drop to Gold Elite, and Gold Elites will drop at most to Silver Elite.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Marriott Bonvoy has just revealed its status soft landing policy for the next membership year, and it’s good news (well, at least for those who don’t requalify for their current status tier).

    Marriott Bonvoy has just revealed its status soft landing policy for the 2027 status year, for situations where someone doesn’t qualify for a particular elite tier based on their activity in 2026. Specifically, elite members who don’t achieve the published criteria to maintain their status will only drop down at most one elite tier.

    In other words, Ambassador Elites will at most drop to Titanium Elite, Titanium Elites will at most drop to Platinum Elite, Platinum Elites will at most drop to Gold Elite, and Gold Elites will drop at most to Silver Elite.

    For what it’s worth, this policy matches Marriott’s historical approach to status soft landings. Before Marriott and Starwood merged, back when Marriott’s loyalty program was named Marriott Rewards, Marriott consistently had a status soft landing policy. With this, Marriott Rewards members never dropped more than one elite tier per year, regardless of their activity.

    Industry observers note that that policy has continued since the fresh program was formed, including for the next year. However, there’s no guarantee this will continue to be the policy in the future. For those curious, the status offered as part of the soft landing also does count toward lifetime elite status. So if you’re downgraded from Titanium to Platinum based on a soft landing, that year of Platinum will add to your total.

    During the pandemic, we saw airline and hotel loyalty programs largely extend elite status several times. This made sense, given the extent to which business travel decreased for many. However, with the huge increase in leisure travel and all the newly introduced ways to earn elite status, we’ve seen elite ranks swell.

    Personally I think the concept of a status soft landing makes a lot of sense. After all, sometimes life conditions change for people, and in many cases those changes are just temporary. If you drop from top tier status to no status, you don’t really have much of an incentive to stay loyal to that hotel group when your travel picks up again.

    It has been revealed that by offering a soft landing, loyalty programs can try to build more of a long term relationship with members, and that’s a positive. We also see some programs allow members to pause their status for a year or extend status as a one-time exception based on life circumstances, and I think that’s a great policy as well.

    Marriott Bonvoy has a generous status soft landing policy for 2027, for those who don’t requalify for status in 2026. If you didn’t requalify for your current status tier with Marriott Bonvoy in 2026, you can expect that you’ll be downgraded at most one status level.

    Yet another giant new cruise ship takes to the sea

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (899 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thepointsguy

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The cruise world welcomed another giant on Wednesday as MSC Cruises took delivery of one of its largest ships ever, the 216,638-ton MSC World Asia.
    • Built at the massive Chantiers de l'Atlantique shipyard in Saint-Nazaire, France, the 20-deck-high, Asia-themed vessel is the third in the line's latest World Class series of ships — by far the biggest ships that MSC Cruises has ever built.
    • Perhaps more notably, it is the tenth largest cruise ship ever built by any line, smaller only than Royal Caribbean's three Icon Class ships and six Oasis Class ships.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The cruise world welcomed another giant on Wednesday as MSC Cruises took delivery of one of its largest ships ever, the 216,638-ton MSC World Asia.

    Built at the massive Chantiers de l'Atlantique shipyard in Saint-Nazaire, France, the 20-deck-high, Asia-themed vessel is the third in the line's latest World Class series of ships — by far the biggest ships that MSC Cruises has ever built.

    Perhaps more notably, it is the tenth largest cruise ship ever built by any line, smaller only than Royal Caribbean's three Icon Class ships and six Oasis Class ships.

    "Our ambition is simple: To give every guest the best holiday ever," MSC Group executive chairman Pierfrancesco Vago noted Wednesday during a dockside ceremony at the Chantiers de l'Atlantique shipyard to mark the vessel's official handover to MSC Cruises.

    MSC Group is the parent tech giant of MSC Cruises and sister brand Explora Journeys, a luxury line.

    "We invested in rethinking spaces, developing newly introduced concepts and reshaping the experience," Vago added during remarks from a stage set up just in front of the MSC World Asia's bow.

    Vago noted that 60% of the spaces on MSC World Asia are either new or significantly redesigned as compared to the two World Class ships already sailing, MSC World Europa and MSC World America.

    Like those two vessels, MSC World Asia has nearly 2,600 rooms and is capable of holding a whopping 6,758 passengers with every berth filled — more than almost any other passenger vessel afloat.

    It also has similarly massive dimensions with a length of 1,093 feet — the equivalent of nearly four football fields stacked end-to-end — and a width of 154 feet.

    But many of its interior and exterior venues, including a sprawling decktop water park with multiple waterslides and a record-setting dry slide that drops 11 decks, are different from what you'll find on the earlier World Class ships in ways major and small.

    Related: The terrifying, record-breaking slide on MSC World Asia.

    Among the most significant changes is the addition of fresh dining and food concepts, including MSC Cruises' first pan-Asian restaurant and a Venchi chocolate and gelato venue.

    Like the earlier World Class vessels, the ship also offers a sushi bar, teppanyaki restaurant, American-style steakhouse and a branch of the Italian chain Eataly (right now found only on MSC World America), among 20 dining options in all.

    In addition to the water park and dry slide, MSC World Asia's top decks offer multiple pool areas; a suspended-over-the-ocean swing ride called The Cliffhangar; and a ropes course.

    Notable interior features include a three-deck-high dining and entertainment zone called the World Galleria, which is covered by one of the largest LED-lit ceilings at sea. An outdoor extension of this area, called the World Promenade, features more dining and entertainment, plus a newly introduced suspended, illuminated Dragon sculpture — part of the ship's Asia theming.

    Related: MSC Cruises cabins and suites guide.

    The arrival of MSC World Asia marks the latest milestone in MSC Cruises' rapid expansion.

    Sources indicate that with the addition of MSC World Asia, the brand now operates 24 ships, up from just 13 vessels as recently as 2017. It has nine more on order.

    The ships on the way include five more World Class vessels scheduled for delivery by 2031. Also coming is a latest class of four somewhat smaller, 180,000-ton vessels that will be known as the Frontier Class.

    Wednesday's delivery ceremony included a ceremonial lowering of the Chantiers de l'Atlantique and French flags in front of attendees and the raising of the MSC Cruises flag as well as the flag of Malta, where the vessel is registered.

    MSC Group chief financial officer Alexa Aponte Vago, who is married to MSC Group executive chairman Pierfrancesco Vago, served as the traditional "godmother" for the event, which included the smashing of a bottle of Champagne against the ship's hull.

    Joining her husband on stage, Alexa Aponte Vago cut a ceremonial blue ribbon to release the bottle of Champagne against the side of the vessel right on the letter C in its name.

    While it included a bottle smash, Wednesday's event was not the vessel's official naming. That will take place Saturday in Le Havre, France, at a much larger event.

    MSC World Asia will then head to the Mediterranean, where it will begin its first cruises with paying passengers on Dec. 4 with a voyage out of Barcelona.

    The ship initially will operate seven-night Mediterranean voyages that include stops in France, Italy, Malta and Spain.

    In November 2027, it will reposition to the Southern Caribbean for seven- to 14-night sailings. The itineraries will include stops in Saint Lucia, Grenada, St. Maarten, Antigua and Barbuda, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Dominica, and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.

    Founded in 1861, the Chantiers d'Atlantique shipyard in St. Nazaire is one of the world's most famous shipyards, known for building many of the world's largest cruise ships as well as naval vessels and wind-powered commercial ships. Notable vessels built at the shipyard include the SS Normandie, SS France, Cunard's Queen Mary 2 and several of Royal Caribbean's Oasis Class ships.

    The shipyard has built 20 vessels for MSC Cruises over the past 25 years.

    It is located at the mouth of the Loire River on the West coast of France.

    Breaking: Chase Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card Review: Are The Benefits Worth The Fee?

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2583 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, the Chase Air Canada Aeroplan® Credit Card is one of the most compelling co-branded airline credit cards out there.
    • In a recent development, so this post is my in-depth Air Canada Aeroplan Card review.
    • Link: Learn more about the Chase Air Canada Aeroplan® Credit Card.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, the Chase Air Canada Aeroplan® Credit Card is one of the most compelling co-branded airline credit cards out there. I’m a huge fan of the Air Canada Aeroplan program — even if you have no connection to Air Canada or Aeroplan, the program is fantastic for partner redemptions, and this card is worth being aware of. And if you do fly Air Canada with any frequency, the perks for travel on the airline are strong.

    In a recent development, so this post is my in-depth Air Canada Aeroplan Card review. Let’s go over all the details, and discuss if the card is worth it.

    Link: Learn more about the Chase Air Canada Aeroplan® Credit Card.

    Before I review the Air Canada Aeroplan Card benefits in detail, here’s a high-level look at everything you need to know about the card:.

    Here are my thoughts on the Air Canada Aeroplan Card’s biggest pros and cons:.

    If you’re thinking about applying for the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card, you’re probably most interested in the welcome bonus it’s presently offering, along with its annual fee and general eligibility rules for getting the card. So let’s get into those details.

    The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card at the moment has the following welcome bonus: Limited Time Offer: Earn up to 80,000 bonus points. Earn 60,000 bonus points after you spend $3,000 on purchases in the first 3 months your account is open. Plus, up to 20,000 more bonus points by earning 50% more bonus points per $1 spent on purchases that normally earn 1 bonus point in the first 2 months from account opening..

    In a recent development, based on my latest miles & points valuations, I consider Aeroplan points to be worth 1.4 cents each. That means the 80,000 points are worth $1,120 to me. However, even if you have a different valuation of these points than I do, you can at least use the “Pay Yourself Back” feature to redeem these points for 1.25 cents each toward a travel purchase, so that’s a pretty high “cash out” value.

    The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card is issued by Chase, and has pretty standard application restrictions:.

    It has been revealed that while Chase doesn’t have a public credit score requirement for the Air Canada Aeroplan Card, you’ll have the best chances of approval if your score is in the good range or higher. That roughly translates to a minimum score of 670. However, people have been approved with lower scores and rejected with higher scores, as it’s one of only many factors that determine card eligibility.

    According to recent reports, the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card has a $195 annual fee. There’s no cost to add authorized people to the card, and their spending will count toward your points balance and any spending thresholds.

    The Air Canada Aeroplan Card has no foreign transaction fees, so it’s a great card to use globally, and possibly even earn bonus rewards on your spending depending on what you’re using the card for.

    In a recent development, the Air Canada Aeroplan Card has a well rounded rewards structure, among the most interesting you’ll find on any airline credit cards. This isn’t just about the number of points that you earn, but also about the additional rewards for spending. Specifically, the Aeroplan Card offers the following:.

    Sources indicate that those are some excellent bonus categories. For what it’s worth, the card offers 1x Aeroplan points on all other purchases, so there are better cards for everyday spending.

    There’s a lot to love about Air Canada Aeroplan points, even if you don’t usually fly Air Canada or travel to Canada. Among other things:.

    Recent findings suggest that I redeem miles through Aeroplan all the time, and consistently get great value. Booking award flights on Air Canada itself rather than other partners isn’t always the best deal, though, especially if you’re booking during a peak travel time, since Air Canada awards use dynamic pricing.

    According to recent reports, the Air Canada Aeroplan Card gives cardmembers plenty of opportunities to earn elite status with Air Canada Aeroplan. You get some status outright just for being a cardmember, and you can earn further status with spending.

    Those who are approved for the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card receive Aeroplan 25K status. This is valid for as long as your account is open. Aeroplan Elite 25K is Air Canada’s entry level status, and includes travel perks with Air Canada, including:.

    Sources indicate that each year, those with the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card also receive 5,000 Status Qualifying Credits (SQCs) to help work toward the next level of Aeroplan status. This is automatic, but as I’ll cover below, you can stack additional credits on top through hitting certain spending thresholds in the calendar year.

    For those curious, below are the Aeroplan elite requirements.

    It has been revealed that beyond the automatic 5,000 SQCs you’ll receive each calendar year just for having the Air Canada Aeroplan Card, you can earn up to 20,000 additional credits by hitting spending thresholds. Here’s how that breaks down:.

    So you can earn a total of 25,000 SQCs each calendar year through the Air Canada Aeroplan Card.

    Whether or not that’s worth it really depends on how much you fly Air Canada, and what the opportunity cost of your credit card spending is.

    Those with the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card can get a one-tier status upgrade to Aeroplan 35K status when they spend $75,000 on the card in a calendar year. You’ll get status for the remainder of the calendar year you qualify and the entire following calendar year.

    Recent findings suggest that if you ask me, the value here is really for someone who is actually loyal to Air Canada. Aeroplan 35K status gets you three complimentary checked bags on Air Canada flights (vs. just one with Aeroplan 25K), 10 eUpgrade credits, and a 3x elite points multiplier on eligible Air Canada or Star Alliance flight bookings, among other things.

    Industry observers note that the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card offers a variety of valuable benefits and credits, beyond the elite status perks covered above. Some of these benefits are offered just for being a cardmember, while others can be earned with spending. The perks are pretty comprehensive, and you’ll find almost everything you could want short of lounge access. So let’s go over those.

    Sources indicate that the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card offers up to $100 in Air Canada statement credits when you make qualifying Air Canada purchases. The credits apply to paid airfare, taxes and fees on award flights, and inflight food and drinks, though onboard Wi-Fi is excluded.

    This breaks down as two credits of up to $50 each, one from January 1 through June 30 and one from July 1 through December 31. If you book cash fares on Air Canada twice a year, this is an easy way to put $100 back in your pocket, and this benefit alone can cover about half of the card’s annual fee.

    As an Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card holder, you can receive a 15% discount on the Aeroplan points required to book an award flight on Air Canada, Air Canada Express, or Air Canada Rouge. In practice, this also seems to work on partner award flights, as long as at least one segment is on Air Canada. The upside here can be absolutely huge, and it’s a great reason to have this card.

    In a recent development, the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card offers a free first checked bag on Air Canada flights for the primary cardmember and up to eight others traveling on the same itinerary. This applies to itineraries with Air Canada, Air Canada Rouge, or Air Canada Express. The value of that could add up pretty rapidly. There’s no need to actually pay for the ticket with the card, as long as you’re the primary cardmember and have your Aeroplan number linked to the reservation.

    According to recent reports, once every four years, the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card offers a credit that’s valid toward a membership with Global Entry, TSA PreCheck, or NEXUS, worth up to $120. These are all programs that can save travelers time at the airport, and potentially even at the border.

    I specifically love that the card also offers a NEXUS credit, since that’s historically something we haven’t seen card issuers offer. NEXUS is arguably the best of the three programs, since it gets you access to Global Entry, TSA PreCheck, and expedited immigration in Canada.

    Admittedly this is probably more interesting in theory than in practice, but I still like where Aeroplan is going with this. Those with the Air Canada Aeroplan Card will automatically have carbon offsets purchased for their flights when redeeming Aeroplan points for an Air Canada flight.

    The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card is a World Elite Mastercard, which comes with certain perks, including a concierge service and presale tickets for eligible events.

    While you’ll want to consult the cardmember agreement for full details, the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card offers a variety of travel protection when paying with the card, including the following:.

    In a recent development, there’s another feature that you’ll find on the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card, which isn’t available on any other airline card. Specifically, the Aeroplan Credit Card offers a Pay Yourself Back feature, whereby cardmembers can apply their Aeroplan points toward travel purchases on any airline, hotel, or rental car, at the rate of 1.25 cents per point, up to 200,000 points per year.

    It has been revealed that this is an incredibly innovative concept, and something that cardmembers may find to be valuable. So whether you want to redeem your points for a stay at a Four Seasons or a flight on JetBlue, the possibilities are endless. It’s also a reason to potentially think of the welcome bonus differently — the bonus points earned with the welcome offer can over time be redeemed toward any recent purchase or even toward the card’s annual fee.

    Sources indicate that the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card also offers the ability to earn priority reward vouchers. Each can be used to get 50% off an eligible Aeroplan award ticket, and is valid for travel on Air Canada or a partner airline.

    You earn these vouchers at the following four annual spending thresholds:.

    These can each be used in the same way, and the value depends on your status:.

    As you can tell, the value here will depend on your status and travel patterns, but there’s potentially quite a bit of value to be had.

    Recent findings suggest that while this is something that most people won’t be able to achieve, I love the concept behind this, and for some it might just be the best deal in travel. The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card offers what I’d consider to be the world’s most valuable companion certificate, for those who spend a million dollars per year on the card.

    If you reach that threshold, you’ll receive an award redemption companion voucher that’s valid globally:.

    We’ve never seen a credit card offer a perk quite this valuable before. Obviously, the spending requirement is massive here, and this would only make sense if you were planning a lot of travel in a particular year. For a certain type of consumer, though, this is an incredible opportunity.

    A few Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card benefits are set to expire on December 31, 2026, so they won’t be around for too much longer. Here’s a quick look:.

    Recent findings suggest that if you already have the card, now is your last chance to take advantage of these perks. Especially with the 10% transfer bonus, it’s worth seeing if an Aeroplan award flight makes sense with your upcoming travel looks so you can get some extra value for your rewards before this perk retires.

    The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card is an innovative product with a substantial welcome bonus, great return on spending, and valuable perks. That’s just about all that I look for in a credit card.

    Airline co-brand credit cards are extremely popular given the allegiance many people have to a particular airline. Admittedly Aeroplan is at a disadvantage in the US market, since not as many people in the US are loyal to Air Canada as they are to American, Delta, or United, for example.

    That being noted, I think the thoughtful value proposition of this card more than makes up for it for Air Canada loyalists. If you like to redeem points for international premium cabin awards, it could be worth applying for this card. Similarly, the card can be worth it for the Pay Yourself Back feature, whereby you can redeem your Aeroplan points however you’d like toward a travel purchase.

    Hopefully most people find value beyond just the bonus, given the excellent rewards structure.

    Industry observers note that arguably the biggest challenge with the Aeroplan Credit Card is how easy Aeroplan points are to earn with other cards that provide more flexibility. Aeroplan is transfer partners with several bank currencies, including Amex Membership Rewards, Bilt Rewards, Capital One, and Chase Ultimate Rewards, and all those currencies can be converted at a 1:1 ratio.

    That means the points are pretty easy to come by, and in many cases there are compelling value propositions on those cards as well.

    If you’re under 5/24, consider these two cards from Chase:.

    If you’re over 5/24, these are some other top Aeroplan Card alternatives to consider:.

    The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card is phenomenal, and easily the most innovative co-branded airline credit card we’ve seen. The card offers a nice welcome bonus, a lucrative rewards structure with a variety of incentives for spending, and comes with great perks, like elite status.

    The Aeroplan program is rewarding in general, but if you don’t fly Air Canada or book award flights through Aeroplan more than once or twice a year, you might want to consider earning flexible points that transfer to this program instead.

    Learn more about the Aeroplan Credit Card.

    For Canadian residents going for high AC status, ignoring this card will cost you. Canadian readers know: AC high status is vital, if you don't want to pay hundreds of thousands of points for longhaul. One needs to earn SQCs. This card's SQC earn rate is higher, compared to the top-tier Canadian AC cards (TD VIP, CIBC VIP, Amex Reserve) so the 25k is faster, cheaper to get.
